Yet personal agents face a privacy-cost-capability tension: cloud models execute multi-step workflows well but expose sensitive intermediate context to external APIs, while local models preserve privacy but remain less reliable. Both settings also pay repeatedly for long skill prompts and growing histories. We propose constant-context skill learning, a context-to-weights framework for recurring agent workflows: reusable procedures are learned in lightweight task-family modules, while inference conditions only on the current observation and a compact state block. A deterministic tracker renders this state block from task progress and supplies aligned subgoal rewards, so each module can be trained with step-level SFT and refined through online RL. Across ALFWorld, WebShop, and SciWorld, our agents achieve strong performance across Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B. With Qwen3-8B, SFT+RL reaches 89.6\% unseen success on ALFWorld, 76.8\% success on WebShop, and 66.4\% unseen success on SciWorld. They match or exceed strong published agent-training results while reducing prompt tokens per turn by 2--7$\times$ relative to controlled ReAct prompting baselines, showing that procedural context can be moved from prompts into weights.

papers.title: PRISM: Perception Reasoning Interleaved for Sequential Decision Making
papers.summary: Scaling LLM-based embodied agents from text-only environments to complex multimodal settings remains a major challenge. Recent work identifies a perception-reasoning-decision gap in standalone Vision-Language Models (VLMs), which often overlook task-critical information. In this paper, we introduce PRISM, a framework that tightly couples perception (VLM) and decision (LLM) through a dynamic question-answer (DQA) pipeline. Instead of passively accepting the VLM's description, the LLM critiques it, probes the VLM with goal-oriented questions, and synthesizes a compact image description. This closed-loop interaction yields a sharp, task-driven understanding of the scene. We evaluate PRISM on the ALFWorld and Room-to-Room (R2R) benchmarks. We show that: (1) PRISM significantly outperforms state-of-the-art image-based models, (2) our Interactive goal-oriented perception pipeline yields systematic and substantial gains, and (3) PRISM is fully automatic, eliminating the need for handcrafted questions or answers.

papers.title: LongSeeker: Elastic Context Orchestration for Long-Horizon Search Agents
papers.summary: Long-horizon search agents must manage a rapidly growing working context as they reason, call tools, and observe information. Naively accumulating all intermediate content can overwhelm the agent, increasing costs and the risk of errors. We propose that effective context management should be adaptive: parts of the agent's trajectory are maintained at different levels of detail depending on their current relevance to the task. To operationalize this principle, we introduce Context-ReAct, a general agentic paradigm for elastic context orchestration that integrates reasoning, context management, and tool use in a unified loop. Context-ReAct provides five atomic operations: Skip, Compress, Rollback, Snippet and Delete, which allow the agent to dynamically reshape its working context, preserving important evidence, summarizing resolved information, discarding unhelpful branches, and controlling context size. We prove that the Compress operator is expressively complete, while the other specialized operators provide efficiency and fidelity guarantees that reduce generation cost and hallucination risk. Building on this paradigm, we develop LongSeeker, a long-horizon search agent fine-tuned from Qwen3-30B-A3B on 10k synthesized trajectories. Across four representative search benchmarks, LongSeeker achieves 61.5% on BrowseComp and 62.5% on BrowseComp-ZH, substantially outperforming Tongyi DeepResearch (43.2% and 46.7%) and AgentFold (36.2% and 47.3%). These results highlight the potential of adaptive context management, showing that agents can achieve more reliable and efficient long-horizon reasoning by actively shaping their working memory.

papers.title: Driver-WM: A Driver-Centric Traffic-Conditioned Latent World Model for In-Cabin Dynamics Rollout
papers.summary: Safe L2/L3 driving automation requires anticipating human-in-the-loop reactions during shared-control transitions. While most driving world models forecast the external environment, in-cabin intelligence remains strictly recognition-oriented and lacks multi-step rollout capabilities for driver dynamics. We introduce Driver-WM, a driver-centric latent world model that rolls out in-cabin dynamics causally conditioned on out-cabin traffic context. This formulation unifies physical kinematics forecasting with auxiliary behavioral and emotional semantic recognition. Operating in a compact latent space constructed from frozen vision-language features, Driver-WM adopts a dual-stream architecture to separately encode external traffic and internal driver states. These streams are directionally coupled via a gated causal injection mechanism, which uses a learned vector gate to modulate external contextual perturbations while strictly enforcing temporal causality. Experiments on AIDE show robust long-horizon forecasting on reactive high-motion clips, improved driver/traffic semantic alignment, and controlled interventions that expose the external-to-internal mechanism.

papers.title: Tree-based Credit Assignment for Multi-Agent Memory System
papers.summary: Memory systems are widely adopted to enhance LLMs for long-horizon tasks, and are commonly organized as multi-agent pipelines with memory building, summarizing, and retrieval agents. To empower this system, existing RL-based methods either apply final downstream task rewards (e.g., QA accuracy) for all agents uniformly, which are coarse and ambiguous, or design task-specific rewards for agents on different subtasks, which require costly annotations (e.g., key evidence) and are difficult to define reliably. To address these limitations, we propose Tree-based Credit Assignment for Multi-Agent Memory Systems (TreeMem), which derives agent-specific credit from the final reward without task-specific annotations. Specifically, TreeMem extends the multi-agent pipeline (builder--summarizer--retrieval) into a tree structure, where each agent's outputs are expanded into multiple subsequent branches. The contribution of each agent is estimated via Monte Carlo averaging over its subsequent branches, capturing how intermediate agent actions may influence the final reward. This converts the coarse final reward into agent-specific optimization signals. These signals are then used to update all agent policies simultaneously, helping heterogeneous agents specialize effectively. Experiments on long-horizon benchmarks show that TreeMem improves memory system performance over strong baselines, validating the effectiveness of tree-structured credit assignment for the multi-agent memory system.

papers.title: SCOUT: Active Information Foraging for Long-Text Understanding with Decoupled Epistemic States
papers.summary: Long-Text Understanding (LTU) at million-token scale requires balancing reasoning fidelity with computational efficiency. Frontier long-context LLMs can process millions of token contexts end-to-end, but they suffer from high token consumption and attention dilution. In parallel, specialized LTU agents often sacrifice fidelity through task-agnostic abstractions like graph construction or indexing. We identify a key insight for LTU: query-relevant information is typically sparse relative to the full document, so effective reasoning should rely on a query-sufficient subset rather than the entire context. To address this, we propose SCOUT, a new paradigm for LTU that shifts from passive processing to active information foraging. It treats the document as an explorable environment and answers from a compact, provenance-grounded epistemic state. Guided by state-level gap diagnosis, SCOUT adaptively alternates between coarse-to-fine exploration and anchored state updates that progressively contract its epistemic state toward query sufficiency. Experiments show that SCOUT matches state-of-the-art proprietary models while reducing token consumption by up to 8x. Moreover, SCOUT remains stable as context length scales, substantially alleviating the practical cost-performance trade-off.

papers.title: Hierarchical Visual Agent: Managing Contexts in Joint Image-Text Space for Advanced Chart Reasoning
papers.summary: Advanced chart question answering requires both precise perception of small visual elements and multi-step reasoning across several subplots. While existing MLLMs are strong at understanding single plots, they often struggle with multi-step reasoning across multiple subplots. We propose HierVA, a hierarchical visual agent framework for chart reasoning that iteratively constructs and updates a working context in a joint image--text space. A high-level manager generates plans and maintains a compact context containing only key information, while specialized workers perform reasoning, gather evidence, and return results. In particular, the agent maintains separate visual and textual contexts, using a zoom-in tool to restrict the visual context. Experiments on the CharXiv reasoning subset demonstrate consistent improvements over strong multimodal baselines, and ablation studies verify that hierarchical architecture, scoped visual context, and distilled context contribute complementary gains.

papers.title: Honest Reporting in Scored Oversight: True-KL0 Property via the Prekopa Principle
papers.summary: We prove the True-KL$_0$ property for a parametric family of heterogeneous scoring rules arising in scored elicitation mechanisms (AI oversight, forecasting, expert surveys). An agent with private type $M>1$, scored through a $d$-dimensional outcome interface, reports to a principal who evaluates via a power-$p$ pseudospherical scoring rule, $p \in (d,d+1)$; $M$ captures the agent's information quality relative to a reference. Honest reporting is dominant-strategy optimal for every $d$ and every $p>1$, without a prior over the agent's type: a consequence of strict properness and identifiability, with a quadratic misreport-loss rate. True-KL$_0$, the property $R(M,p,d)<1$ for all $M>1$, $d \in \{2,3,4\}$, $p \in (d,d+1)$, is the quantitative core: $R$ is the Rayleigh quotient of the radial misreport channel of an annular oversight model, and True-KL$_0$ certifies a uniform curvature-domination margin for that channel: $1-R \ge 0.26$ ($R \le 0.7324$, semi-rigorous numerical certificate). Two structural tools drive the proof: (i) a substitution $y=(x+1)/(x-1)$ rewrites the loss integral $I_L$ as $\int_1^M F(y)(M^2-y^2)^{d/2} dy$ with $M$-independent weight $F(y)>0$; (ii) log-concavity of $I_L$ in $M$: algebraic for $d=2$ up to a small certified compact verification, via Prekopa's theorem plus semi-rigorous certificates for $d \in \{3,4\}$. True-KL$_0$ then follows from elementary tail bounds plus a certified bound on $M \in [1.001, 20]$. We also characterise the dimensional boundary: True-KL$_0$ holds for all $p \in (d,d+1)$ when $d \le 4$; $d=5$ is the unique transition, with $p_{crit}(5) \in [5.5718, 5.5750]$ (mpmath, not interval-certified); for $d=6,7$ (and conjecturally all $d \ge 6$) no threshold exists: the bound fails at every sampled $p \in (d,d+1)$.

papers.title: ProgramBench: Can Language Models Rebuild Programs From Scratch?
papers.summary: Turning ideas into full software projects from scratch has become a popular use case for language models. Agents are being deployed to seed, maintain, and grow codebases over extended periods with minimal human oversight. Such settings require models to make high-level software architecture decisions. However, existing benchmarks measure focused, limited tasks such as fixing a single bug or developing a single, specified feature. We therefore introduce ProgramBench to measure the ability of software engineering agents to develop software holisitically. In ProgramBench, given only a program and its documentation, agents must architect and implement a codebase that matches the reference executable's behavior. End-to-end behavioral tests are generated via agent-driven fuzzing, enabling evaluation without prescribing implementation structure. Our 200 tasks range from compact CLI tools to widely used software such as FFmpeg, SQLite, and the PHP interpreter. We evaluate 9 LMs and find that none fully resolve any task, with the best model passing 95\% of tests on only 3\% of tasks. Models favor monolithic, single-file implementations that diverge sharply from human-written code.

papers.title: GeoDecider: An Evidence-Grounded Agent for Geological Interpretation via Deliberative Reasoning
papers.summary: Geological interpretation infers subsurface properties and structures from indirect geophysical observations. Well-log classification provides a measurable setting by assigning geological classes to depth-indexed petrophysical records. The task is difficult because different subsurface units may exhibit similar logging responses, whereas accurate interpretation often depends on local measurements, depth-wise context, domain knowledge, and reasonable transitions between neighboring layers. Existing automated methods mainly follow fixed prediction pipelines, leaving little room to gather additional evidence for difficult samples. In this work, we propose GeoDecider, an evidence-grounded agent for deliberative geological interpretation. GeoDecider retains efficient numerical prediction as the first stage, then selectively invokes tool-assisted reasoning for difficult intervals. A lightweight classifier produces point-wise predictions and estimates sample difficulty from its prediction scores. High-difficulty points act as routing anchors, triggering interval-level analysis so that nearby observations can be examined together. For each activated interval, specialized tools build an Evidence Profile that summarizes geological knowledge, depth-wise trends, previous predictions from the same well, and similar cases retrieved from training wells. Three complementary scientific views generate candidate interpretations. GeoDecider compares their supporting evidence, resolves disagreements, then applies geology-informed checks on continuity, boundary cues, and petrophysical consistency. Experiments on four public well-log benchmarks show that GeoDecider consistently outperforms representative baselines, demonstrating the value of selective evidence gathering and deliberative reasoning for geological interpretation.~\footnote{Our code is available at https://github.com/Xiaoyu-Tao/GeoDecider}

papers.title: MemFlow: Intent-Driven Memory Orchestration for Small Language Model Agents
papers.summary: Modern language agents must operate over long-horizon, multi-turn histories, yet deploying such agents with Small Language Models (SLMs) remains fundamentally difficult. Full-context prompting causes context overflow, flat retrieval exposes the model to noisy evidence, and open-ended agentic loops are unreliable under limited reasoning capacity. We argue that a substantial portion of SLM memory failure arises from mismatched memory operations: different query types demand categorically different retrieval strategies, evidence transformations, and context budgets that SLMs cannot reliably self-orchestrate through open-ended reasoning. We introduce MemFlow, a training-free memory orchestration framework that externalizes memory planning from the SLM. A Router Agent classifies each query by intent and dispatches it to the Memory Agent, which executes one of three specialized tiers (Profile Lookup, Targeted Retrieval, or Deep Reasoning) and assembles the resulting evidence under a dynamic, tier-aware token budget. An Answer Agent then generates a response from this compact context, and a Validator Agent optionally retries with a heavier memory tier when the response is not supported by the provided evidence. This route-then-compile design avoids tool-selection hallucination and reasoning loops while keeping the answer context compact. Evaluated on a frozen Qwen3-1.7B backbone across long-horizon memory benchmarks - LongMemEval, LoCoMo, and LongBench - MemFlow improves accuracy by nearly 2x over full-context SLM baselines. These results suggest that structured intent routing and deterministic evidence preparation can make limited-capacity models substantially more effective in resource-constrained long-horizon agents.

papers.title: S^2tory: Story Spine Distillation for Movie Script Summarization
papers.summary: Movie scripts pose a fundamental challenge for automatic summarization due to their non-linear, cross-cut narrative structure, which makes surface-level saliency methods ineffective at preserving core story progression. To address this, we introduce S^2tory (Story Spine Distillation), a narratology-grounded framework that leverages character development trajectories to identify plot nuclei, the essential events that drive the narrative forward, while filtering out peripheral satellite events that merely enrich atmosphere or emotion. Our Narrative Expert Agent (NEAgent) performs theory-constrained reasoning, whose distilled knowledge conditions a small model to identify plot nuclei. Another model then uses these plot nuclei to generate the summary. Experiments on the MovieSum dataset demonstrate state-of-the-art semantic fidelity at approximately 3.5x compression, and zero-shot evaluation on BookSum confirms strong out-of-domain generalization. Human evaluation further validates that narratological theory provides an indispensable foundation for modeling complex, non-linear narratives.

papers.title: Quantitative Sobolev Approximation Bounds for Neural Operators with Empirical Validation on Burgers Equation
papers.summary: Neural operators have emerged as a powerful tool for learning mappings between infinite-dimensional function spaces. However, their approximation properties in Sobolev norms remain poorly quantified, even though these norms control both function values and derivatives and are the natural metrics for PDE well-posedness, stability, and generalization. We develop a functional-analytic framework for operator learning in Sobolev spaces and connect it to the numerical behavior of Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs) on a prototypical PDE. First, for a continuous nonlinear operator $\mathcal{G}: H^{s}(D)\to H^{t}(D')$ with $s > d/2$ and inputs restricted to a compact subset of $H^{s}(D)$, we prove that $\mathcal{G}$ can be uniformly approximated in $H^{t}$-norm by a neural operator with $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-d/s})$ trainable parameters. This yields an explicit complexity--error relation of the form $\|\mathcal{G}-\mathcal{G}_θ\|_{H^{t}} \lesssim C N^{-s/d}$. We then study the one-dimensional viscous Burgers solution operator $\mathcal{G}: u_{0}\mapsto u(\cdot,1)$ on a bounded $H^{1}$-ball and train FNOs with an $H^{1}$-loss. Across a sweep of model sizes, we obtain test $H^{1}$-errors down to $\mathcal{O}(10^{-7})$ and relative errors of order $10^{-3}$, with predictions accurately matching both solutions and spatial derivatives on held-out data. A log-log plot of Sobolev error versus parameter count exhibits an approximate power law $\|\mathcal{G}-\mathcal{G}_θ\|_{H^{1}} \approx C N^{-α}$ with empirical exponent $α\approx 1.4$, and long-horizon training reveals optimization instabilities in large FNOs, providing quantitative evidence that Sobolev-space approximation theory meaningfully predicts neural-operator scaling behavior.

papers.title: Phionyx: A Deterministic AI Runtime Architecture with Structured State Management and Pre-Response Governance
papers.summary: We present Phionyx, a deterministic AI runtime architecture derived from the broader Echoism interaction framework that introduces a governance-first approach to AI engineering: treating large language model (LLM) outputs as noisy sensor measurements rather than direct decisions. Unlike probabilistic agents, Phionyx enforces deterministic state evolution via a structured state vector governed by deterministic state-evolution equations, enabling reproducible behavior in applications requiring auditability and governance. The architecture integrates three layers: (1) a deterministic evaluation kernel processing noisy sensor measurements through a canonical 46-block pipeline, (2) a unified safety layer providing pre-response control and architectural privacy enforcement, and (3) a semantic time-based memory system implementing impact-weighted cache eviction. Experimental validation on single-instance deployments demonstrates approximately 31% reduction in computational overhead vs. post-hoc filtering (at 30% unsafe input ratio, simulated cost model) and up to 24% improvement in high-value data retention vs. LRU (72% vs. FIFO, same cache capacity, benchmark-verified), deterministic execution verified across 100 repeated runs with zero variance in control signals (hash-verified), and zero unplanned restarts in single-instance deployment testing (see Appendix C for methodology and scope). This paper presents the architecture, its analytic structure, and scoped experimental evidence; generalization to distributed or multi-tenant deployments remains future work.

papers.title: Autonomous LLM Agent Worms: Cross-Platform Propagation, Automated Discovery and Temporal Re-Entry Defense
papers.summary: Autonomous LLM agents operate as long-running processes with persistent workspaces, memory files, scheduled task state, and messaging integrations. These features create a new propagation risk: attacker-influenced content can be written into persistent agent state, re-enter the LLM decision context through scheduled autoloading, and drive high-risk actions including configuration changes and cross-agent transmission. We present the first systematic framework for automated analysis of persistent worm propagation in file-backed multi-agent LLM ecosystems. SSCGV, our automated source-code graph analyzer, traces data flow from file I/O to LLM context injection points and ranks carriers by context injection position without manual analysis. SRPO, our summary-resilient payload optimizer, generates worm payloads robust to LLM-mediated summarization and paraphrasing across multi-hop communication. Evaluated on three production agent frameworks, we demonstrate zero-click autonomous propagation, 3-hop cross-platform transmission without platform-specific adaptation, inter-agent privilege escalation, and data exfiltration. We identify two empirical insights: user prompt carriers achieve higher attack compliance than system prompt carriers, and read operations represent the primary integrity threat in LLM-mediated systems. To defend against this class of attacks, we develop RTW-A, proven under a formal No Persistent Worm Propagation theorem. RTW blocks write-before-exposed-read re-entry; sealed configuration protects static files; typed memory promotion prevents untrusted summaries from entering trusted memory; and capability attenuation limits high-risk actions after external reads. These mechanisms eliminate the persistence, re-entry, action chain while preserving ordinary workflows. Affected systems are anonymized pending coordinated disclosure.

papers.title: A stiff limit of non-homogeneous conservation laws for crowd motion modeling
papers.summary: We propose a new approach for crowd motion models where the density constraint can only slow down the motion of each agent, with no effect on those agents who are not in a saturated area or who have no saturated density ''in front'' of them. This is done by means of a limit of conservation laws inspired by the equations used for traffic as in Follow the leader-type models. We study the asymptotics of the solutions of these conservation laws in a certain asymptotic regime, and obtain a PDE at the limit of a whole new type. One of the main goals of the paper is to prove uniform BV estimates on the density, and thus strong compactness to prove the existence of solutions to this limit equation. We also discuss the qualitative behavior of solutions, provide numerical illustrations both in dimension 1 and 2, and establish the new entropy inequalities associated with this limit equation.

papers.title: AOCI: Symbolic-Semantic Indexing for Practical Repository-Scale Code Understanding with LLMs
papers.summary: Large language models struggle with understanding codebases beyond a certain scale -- repositories with hundreds of thousands of lines of code. Existing methods -- retrieval, summarization, agent exploration -- each construct a different view at query time. The view varies between runs, and what persists is typically ad-hoc rather than systematic. This paper introduces AOCI (AI-Oriented Code Indexing): a symbolic-semantic repository representation -- a structured blueprint that an LLM can read in a single pass to gain a complete repository-level picture of the system's architecture, dependencies, and key design decisions before any task. An AOCI index consists of encoding rules followed by entries, with one entry per code unit (file or database table). Each entry pairs a symbolic tag with semantic content. The symbolic component provides architectural coordinates; the semantic component carries function, dependencies, and constraints. Together they form a consistent, stable representation of the entire system. Index maintenance is incremental: when code changes, only affected entries are regenerated under protocol rules. The AOCI Platform automates this process, keeping the blueprint aligned with the code. We evaluated AOCI on four projects across three LLMs and six context conditions (2,160 evaluations). AOCI outperforms all deployable baselines and ranks second only to the Oracle upper bound in overall accuracy. On 19 industrial tasks across five systems, AOCI produced zero final-state defects, while three mainstream agent-based tools introduced defects in 12 tasks and consumed 4--130$\times$ more tokens ($p < 0.001$). The advantage grows with task complexity.

papers.title: HeavySkill: Heavy Thinking as the Inner Skill in Agentic Harness
papers.summary: Recent advances in agentic harness with orchestration frameworks that coordinate multiple agents with memory, skills, and tool use have achieved remarkable success in complex reasoning tasks. However, the underlying mechanism that truly drives performance remains obscured behind intricate system designs. In this paper, we propose HeavySkill, a perspective that views heavy thinking not only as a minimal execution unit in orchestration harness but also as an inner skill internalized within the model's parameters that drives the orchestrator to solve complex tasks. We identify this skill as a two-stage pipeline, i.e., parallel reasoning then summarization, which can operate beneath any agentic harness. We present a systematic empirical study of HeavySkill across diverse domains. Our results show that this inner skill consistently outperforms traditional Best-of-N (BoN) strategies; notably, stronger LLMs can even approach Pass@N performance. Crucially, we demonstrate that the depth and width of heavy thinking, as a learnable skill, can be further scaled via reinforcement learning, offering a promising path toward self-evolving LLMs that internalize complex reasoning without relying on brittle orchestration layers.

papers.title: Optimal (Randomized) Compact Routing Schemes
papers.summary: Compact routing schemes route messages along short paths while every vertex stores little information. We study the trade-off between the stretch and the storage of compact routing schemes in undirected graphs, in four models: labeled and name-independent schemes, with average or worst-case local storage. We improve the best known stretch in all four models. Our main result is a labeled routing scheme with expected stretch $2k-1$ and $\widetilde O(n^{1/k})$ average local storage, in which only the routing is randomized. Under the Erdős girth conjecture, no scheme with this storage has stretch below $2k-1$, so our scheme is optimal, up to polylogarithmic factors in the storage. With deterministic routing, we obtain stretch $\approx2.47k$, the best known deterministic stretch with average storage. Worst-case local storage is the classical setting of compact routing. The leading coefficient $4$ in the stretch $4k-5$ of Thorup and Zwick~[SPAA'01] was improved only by Chechik~[PODC'13], to $\approx3.68$ in unweighted graphs. In unweighted graphs, we obtain expected stretch $(\frac83k+O(1),O(k))$, and deterministic stretch $\approx3.05k$. Name-independent routing is harder, since the source knows only the name of the destination. The best known stretch with $\widetilde O(n^{1/k})$ local storage in unweighted graphs was $96k$, by Abraham, Gavoille, and Malkhi~[DISC'04]. We improve it by more than a factor of $8$. With average storage, we obtain expected stretch $4k-5$, which matches the labeled scheme of Thorup and Zwick. With worst-case storage in unweighted graphs, we obtain expected stretch $(8k+O(1),O(k))$. All our schemes for unweighted graphs extend to weighted graphs with a small loss in the stretch, and still improve the previous unweighted bounds.

papers.title: A Unified AI Framework for Rapid and Accurate Waveform Generation of Compact Binary Coalescences
papers.summary: The astrophysical discovery potential of future gravitational wave detectors will hinge on accurate and rapid waveform generation. Third generation detectors are expected to observe many long duration compact binary coalescence signals that can probe binary formation and evolution as well as the nature of matter under extreme conditions. We develop a unified framework that combines physical modeling with deep learning. The framework uses an analytic residual spectral representation, shared learning, and decoders for each binary type. It generates waveforms for binary black holes, binary neutron stars, and neutron star black hole binaries, providing a single unified generator for all compact binary coalescences. The generated waveforms include the physical effects described by each reference model, such as spin precession, higher order modes, matter effects, and postmerger radiation for binary neutron stars. The waveforms span hundreds to thousands of cycles, with mean mismatches ranging from $5.89\times10^{-4}$ to $5.34\times10^{-2}$ relative to the reference waveforms. Batch generation achieves a maximum speedup of about 1800 over reference waveform generation.

papers.title: Ergodic full measures and entropy spectrum for countable observables on compact spaces
papers.summary: We investigate conditions and obstructions for the existence of ergodic full measures in the context of countable observables on compact spaces. Extending the theory in a unified way, we are able to show a complete picture via thermodynamic formalism for symbolic, uniformly hyperbolic and related systems. We prove conditional variational principles for the topological entropy, showing good approximations by ergodic full measures, and we give conditions where we precisely get ergodic full measures. In contrast with the case with a finite number of observables, new phenomena appear: we exhibit explicit examples of level sets with a null measure with respect to any invariant measure but having large entropy. On the other hand, based on induced ergodic systems in the sense of Kakutani-Rokhlin and heavily utilizing the formalism for countable Markov shifts, we go beyond the classical thermodynamic approach and show a different way of building ergodic full measures. Additionally, we study the regularity and shape of the entropy spectrum and, in the end, we also give some applications of the main conditional variational principles.

papers.title: Approximate Synthetic Spectra of Quantum Systems Associated with Compact Lie Groups
papers.summary: How can noncommuting quantum observables retain the geometry of a classical phase space? Motivated by Mumford's question on approximately macroscopically unique (AMU) states and the work of Lin and Wang, we study synthetic spectra of position--momentum and angular-momentum systems. Under the hypotheses of their AMU theorems, nonempty synthetic spectra yield AMU states. For sufficiently small $\hbar$, the position--momentum spectrum fills the plane, while the angular-momentum spectrum contains any prescribed ball. The latter calculation leads to compact Lie groups: we prove that highest-weight coadjoint orbits lie in regional synthetic spectra under an explicit variance bound. Function-space representations of $SU(n)$, $SO(n)$, and $Sp(n)$ provide further examples.

papers.title: Feynman Propagators on Exponentially Decaying Perturbations of Stationary Spacetimes with Compact Cauchy Surface
papers.summary: In this paper, we construct Feynman propagators on exponentially decaying perturbations of stationary spacetime with compact Cauchy surface. The propagators are defined as parametrices of the wave operator on exponentially weighted Sobolev spaces defined by complex contours $Γ$. We then apply this theory to the computation of indexes of Dirac operators using a continuous Wick-like rotation to relate it to the Riemannian case.

papers.title: Schrodinger group along the horocycles and Egorov's theorem on compact hyperbolic surfaces
papers.summary: In this paper, we study Egorov's theorem for Laplacian eigenfunctions on compact hyperbolic surfaces in Zelditch's quantization. In this quantization, the remainder in Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is given explicitly by the second derivatives of the symbols along the weak stable foliation of the geodesic flow. Forward in time, we show that Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid to all logarithmic times, far beyond the Ehrenfest time T_E=|log h|/2, where h going to 0 is the semiclassical parameter. Backward in time, we introduce the Schrodinger group along the stable horocycles, which absorbs the exponentially growing part of the remainder. We show that Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid up to -T_E+T_h for any Th going to infinity with 0<=T_h<=T_E. Moreover, the limit of the remainder in Egorov's theorem at the Ehrenfest time -T_E is exactly the difference between the semiclassical measure and the Liouville measure, tested against the symbols propagated by the Schrodinger group. Consequently, Egorov's theorem for a sequence of eigenfunctions holds at -T_E (and in fact, at -T_E-T for any fixed T in R if and only if the sequence tends to be equidistributed in the phase space. Thus, the quantum unique ergodicity (QUE) conjecture is equivalent to this Egorov property holding for every eigenbasis. Furthermore, QUE holds with a polynomial rate if and only if Egorov's theorem holds at -T_E with a polynomial remainder. In this case, Egorov's theorem holds beyond -T_E with a polynomial remainder, and the stronger the rate is in QUE, the longer the time is in Egorov's theorem.

papers.title: Lattice spin systems coupled to a compact U(1) gauge field with negative gauge coupling favoring frustration
papers.summary: We investigate the phase diagram and nature of the phase transitions of three-dimensional compact lattice Abelian Higgs models with negative gauge coupling. These models describe multicomponent complex scalar fields coupled to a compact U(1) gauge field. Negative gauge coupling favors frustrated plaquette configurations, competing with the tendency of the matter ferromagnetic-like interaction to suppress frustration. Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analyses of models with one- and two-component scalar fields of unit charge reveal a substantially richer phase structure than at nonnegative gauge coupling. For two components, the O(3) transition line associated with gauge-invariant bilinear ordering extends into the negative-coupling region, and turns into a first-order transition line with decreasing $K$, toward the fully-frustrated $K\to -\infty$ limit. An analogous first-order transition line is also found for the one-component scalar matter with negative gauge coupling. Both one- and two-component models exhibit two additional continuous transition lines at sufficiently large matter coupling. Their energy-cumulant scaling is consistent with three-dimensional Ising and XY critical exponents, suggesting topological transitions in the $\mathbb Z_2$ and XY gauge universality classes, respectively. These results uncover additional phases generated by the competition between matter ordering and dynamical gauge frustration, whose physical characterization remains an open question.

papers.title: Compact holography via polarized IKKT
papers.summary: The polarized IKKT matrix model is a $U(N)$ supersymmetric matrix integral proposed to be dual to an $N$ D-instanton sector of Euclidean type IIB string theory. We show a direct path from matrix model saddles to supergravity saddles: matrix model resolvent $\to$ holomorphic function $\to$ 2D Coulomb potential $\to$ 4D Coulomb potential $\to$ supergravity fields, where the last step was previously described. Here, the 2D electrostatics picture is an exact finite $N$ reformulation of a localization deformation of the matrix model that gives a constrained gas of dipoles in a background field. We show a matching between supergravity and matrix model on-shell actions and protected observables for all saddles. We show that the supergravity saddles have a compact and non-singular metric in string frame with the Einstein frame asymptotic region replaced by a pointlike D-instanton source. We provide evidence that the physics of particular gravity saddles can be obtained through restricting the domain of the matrix model integral to a basin associated with the corresponding matrix model saddle. We describe certain large $N$ decoupling limits where families of the saddles decouple from the rest to give the gravity duals of certain higher-dimensional field theories.

papers.title: Ly$α$ in Compact Broad-Line Emitters, Including Little Red Dots, Is More Closely Linked to the Host Galaxy than to the Broad-Line Nucleus
papers.summary: JWST has found many faint broad-line AGN at $z>4$, but it is unclear whether the Ly$α$ we see from them comes from the accreting black hole or from its host galaxy. The answer matters for how these sources are interpreted and for how many ionizing photons they release. We use deep JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy from the DIVER program to measure Ly$α$ in 12 compact broad-line emitters (CBEs) at $z=4.2$--5.5 in GOODS-N. CBEs include little red dots (LRDs), little blue dots, and other broad-line AGN. Six are detected in Ly$α$. Every source shows a broad-line region, yet Ly$α$ does not follow it: the sources with the strongest H$α$ relative to the UV include weak detections and nondetections, and every detected Ly$α$ line (FWHM $\approx300$--1000~km~s$^{-1}$) is narrower than broad H$α$ (1100--3300~km~s$^{-1}$). Instead, Ly$α$ appears to track the host galaxy. We model the AGN-subtracted host with a dust-attenuated SED fit. Including the upper limits, the observed Ly$α$ follows the Ly$α$ production in this host model more closely than it follows H$α$/UV, in both equivalent width and luminosity. Every detection exceeds its host-model value by a factor of 1.5--18, leaving room for a nuclear contribution. The black hole is visible in these sources, but the Ly$α$ we observe is more closely tied to its host. The median effective Ly$α$ escape fraction of the detections is only 0.09, which suggests that ionizing escape from CBEs is typically modest and varies widely.

papers.title: Tiny Galaxies, Mighty Nitrogen: Linking Chemical Anomalies to Compact Galaxies at High Redshift using JWST/JADES
papers.summary: The origin of anomalous chemical enrichment in high-redshift galaxies discovered by JWST remains a key question in galaxy evolution. Enhanced nitrogen abundances have been identified in several galaxies at early cosmic times, but the physical conditions driving this enrichment, and their connection to galaxy morphology, remain unclear. We test whether morphologically compact galaxies at 4 < z < 7 show stronger chemical anomalies than extended systems. Using JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopic data, we construct samples of compact and extended galaxies and analyse their rest-frame spectra. We stack the spectra of each population and measure key UV and optical emission lines. We detect nitrogen emission in the compact galaxy stack, including NIV], and [NII], while also detecting key carbon and oxygen lines. The detection of [OIII]λ4363 enables a direct-Te determination of the oxygen abundance. From these measurements, we infer chemical abundance ratios, including log(N/O) and log(C/O). We find that compact galaxies exhibit elevated log(N/O) (by ~ 0.7 dex) and log(C/O) (by ~ 0.5 dex) abundance ratios relative to extended systems. The abundance patterns of compact galaxy stacks are comparable to those of previously identified individual nitrogen-enhanced galaxies at high redshift and second-generation globular-cluster stars in the Milky Way. These results suggest a possible link between galaxy compactness and chemical enrichment pathways in the early Universe. Deeper JWST NIRSpec IFU observations of compact high-redshift galaxies will be crucial for determining the origin, spatial distribution, and evolutionary significance of these abundance patterns.

papers.title: Jets and winds from the most powerful compact object in NGC 5408
papers.summary: Super-critical accretion onto stellar-mass compact objects is sometimes revealed by ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs). In other cases, X-rays are heavily obscured along our line of sight, but a super-Eddington accretion power can be indirectly revealed by multiband studies. We have identified a candidate super-critical source in NGC 5408 (labelled X-2). We argue that: it is powered by accretion; it is among the most powerful in the local universe, despite its apparent X-ray faintness; it has exceptional optical properties (both in the continuum and in the lines). We carried out a multiband imaging and spectral study with the ATCA, the VLA, HST, the VLT and Chandra. We found an unresolved source with: variable radio emission (5-GHz luminosity of a few x 10^{35} erg/s); red optical continuum with absolute mag M_{V,0} = -9.1, M_{I,0} = -10.6; exceptionally broad low-ionization emission lines (FWHM ~ 1700 km/s) with P-Cygni profiles; narrow, photoionized emission lines including strong He II 4686; point-like hard X-rays; marginally resolved soft X-rays. We also found an ~20-pc He^{++} nebula near X-2, associated with candidate Wolf-Rayet stars. The optical continuum declined by 2 mag between 2010 and 2024, as did the intensity of broad and narrow lines. We argue that the system is powered by the radiative and mechanical output of a super-Eddington stellar mass BH, with an accretion power >~10^{40} erg/s. We propose that X-2 is a Compton-thick ULX seen at high inclination, with a flaring jet and X-ray emission emerging from the polar funnel. We argue that the optical continuum and the broad emission lines are signatures of an optically thick outflow, launched either from the accretion disk, or from an LBV-like donor star, or, more speculatively, caused by the elusive phase of common envelope ejection. We suggest that we are looking at a short-lived phase of hyper-Eddington accretion.

papers.title: VizDAGuide: Misleading Chart Question Answering in Compact Vision Language Models via DAG-Structured Supervision
papers.summary: Misleading charts can lead vision-language models to conclusions that conflict with underlying data. Existing work focuses on inference-time strategies, while training-time supervision remains less explored. We present VizDAGuide, a DAG-structured supervision method for misleading-chart question answering. The method represents intermediate reasoning states and their dependencies as a directed acyclic graph, assigns supervision weights according to their roles, and serializes the graph into a unified training target for open-ended and multiple-choice QA with single-pass inference. Experiments on two benchmarks across Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5 models show improvements over a content- and weight-matched Linear CoT-SFT baseline on both answer formats. Process-level evaluation shows gains in grounding and operation execution, while ablations indicate that dependency structure and weighted supervision are most effective when combined. These results support DAG-structured weighted supervision for misleading-chart question answering.

papers.title: A Compact Statistical View of Musical-Instrument Directivity
papers.summary: Directivity is a defining feature of musical-instrument radiation and is known to vary strongly with frequency. With the growing availability of measured directivity datasets and their use in sound-field simulation and spatial audio, there is a practical need for representations that are both compact and comparable across sources. This work addresses that need by proposing a statistically grounded description of frequency-dependent directivity that reduces complex radiation patterns to a small set of meaningful descriptors. The approach enables directivity patterns to be summarized in an interpretable way and compared consistently across frequency bands, even when the radiation is not well described by a single dominant direction. The resulting representation supports tasks such as analysis, categorization, and model building, providing a bridge between detailed measurements and higher-level descriptors useful for musical acoustics and audio rendering. Experiments on a corpus of 41 orchestral instruments show that the proposed method preserves the distance geometry well while reducing the full order-4, 30-band corpus from about 492~kB to about 100~kB in double-precision storage.

papers.title: The Brin-Katok local entropy formula for non-compact random dynamical systems and an application
papers.summary: In this paper, we establish the classical Brin-Katok local entropy formula for $C^1$ random dynamical systems on a complete Riemannian manifold (possibly non-compact) under a mild integrability condition. The proof depends on the constructions of measurable partitions adapted to asymptotically varying radii and finite measurable partitions with null-boundaries. As an application, under additional integrability assumptions, we obtain the Margulis-Ruelle inequality for $C^2$ random dynamical systems on complete non-compact Riemannian manifolds. Furthermore, we also construct a counterexample showing that the integrability condition above cannot in general be omitted.

papers.title: Less but Sufficient: Relation Knowledge Selects Compact Knowledge-Graph Contexts, and What External Checks Can and Cannot Catch
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) read knowledge-graph facts ranked by relevance, leaving open whether they suffice or conflict. Our checks use relation knowledge, written by hand or learned from training questions labelled with their relation paths. It selects a compact context of facts yielding an answer, and derives it; a derivability check tests whether an answer follows, a consistency check whether facts conflict, and a validation-chosen routing gate decides where the derived answer replaces the LLM's. Seven open LLMs read the compact context better in exact match than relevance-ranked facts; on ComplexWebQuestions (CWQ) they match SubgraphRAG's facts at a quarter of the prompt tokens, and stronger LLMs read SubgraphRAG's better. Where the routing gate passes, ours leads SubgraphRAG's in exact match in all 53 LLM, benchmark and prompt settings. A precision gate, returning the derived answer only when the check passes with exactly one derived entity, answered 18 and 5 percent of held-out WebQSP and CWQ questions in a pre-specified test, right for 90 and 96 percent. The consistency check judges facts by path evidence only where another path joins their entities, true of 2.5 percent of named-entity facts in our compact WebQSP and CWQ contexts.

papers.title: The ball fixed point property for continuous functions on locally compact spaces
papers.summary: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and $p\in K$. We prove that the Banach space $C(K,p)=\{f\in C(K,\mathbb R):f(p)=0\}$ fails the ball fixed point property (BFPP) whenever $p$ is non-isolated, answering a question of Avilés, Japón, Lennard, Martínez-Cervantes and Stawski. Consequently, $C_0(L)$ fails the BFPP for every noncompact locally compact Hausdorff space $L$. Together with Barroso's characterization for $C(K)$, this yields complete topological classifications of the BFPP for $C_0(L)$ and $C(K,p)$. We also resolve a second question of Avilés et al., showing that the BFPP of $C(K)$ implies that of $C(K,p)$ for every compact Hausdorff space $K$ and every $P$-point $p\in K$ if and only if there are no measurable cardinals.

papers.title: Dynamically defined bulges reveal that early-type galaxies with compact bulges host more massive black holes
papers.summary: We revisit the $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}$ relation for early-type galaxies by introducing a uniform bulge defined by dynamical decomposition. From the set of nearby galaxies with accurately measured black hole masses, we select 30 early-type galaxies that have been observed with wide-field integral-field unit instruments (MUSE, ATLAS3D, or PPAK). For each galaxy, we construct an orbit-superposition Schwarzschild model and obtain its stellar orbit distribution. In this framework, we define the bulge uniformly as comprising stellar orbits with circularity $λ_z < 0.7$ (or, in an alternative definition, $λ_z < 0.2$) and lying within $r < 3$ kpc. From these orbits, we reconstruct the spatial density distribution of the bulge and measure its mass ($M_{bulge}$), size ($R_{bulge}$) and surface density slope ($γ_{bulge}$). We find that the dynamical bulge defined by $λ_z < 0.7$ yields masses that are systematically consistent with the photometric bulge masses. Comparing to the bulge from photometric decomposition, using this dynamical bulge definition slightly decreases the scatter around the best-fitting from 0.56 to 0.47. More interestingly, we identify a clear trend: at a given bulge mass, galaxies hosting more compact bulges (i.e. smaller bulge sizes or steeper bulge density slopes) systematically contain more massive black holes; eight outliers show overmassive BHs together with ultra-compact bulges. We interpret this as direct observational evidence that the $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}$ relation evolves over a galaxy's merger history, with that history imprinted in bulge compactness. Incorporating compactness via an $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}-R_{e, bulge}$ (or $γ_{bulge}$) relation brings the outliers into agreement and reduces the overall scatter of the sample to $\sim 0.3$.

papers.title: Profile decomposition, strict binding and global compactness for a critical Grushin embedding
papers.summary: We study attainment of the best constant in \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^{m+n}} \bigl(|\nabla_xu|^2+|x|^2|\nabla_yu|^2+a|u|^2\bigr) \geq S_a\left(\int_{\mathbb R^{m+n}} (1+|x|^2)^{n/(Q-2)}|u|^q\right)^{2/q}, \end{equation*} where \(m,n\geq1\), \(Q=m+2n\), \(q=2Q/(Q-2)\), and \(a>0\). Using annular interpolation and a transverse-average recurrence with \(L^q\) contraction \(2^{-m/q}\), we decompose bounded sequences into finite, Grushin and Euclidean profiles. Energy and critical mass split, with a power bound in the number of profiles on the remaining mass. We prove compactness of normalized minimizing sequences modulo \(y\)-translations under \(S_a<\min\{S_G,a^{n/Q}S_E(1)\}\), where \(S_G\) and \(S_E(1)\) are the tangent constants. The strict-binding set is empty or an open interval; we prove nonemptiness for \(n=1\) and even \(m\geq6\). At finite positive endpoints of a nonempty binding interval, we characterize attainment by first-order binding gaps. We obtain a finite critical-profile decomposition of Palais--Smale sequences with a remainder vanishing in energy.

papers.title: pico-WAM: Evaluating Counterfactual Prediction and Planning Error in a Compact World Action Model
papers.summary: When a World Action Model fails at control, is the bottleneck proposal generation or trajectory scoring? We introduce pico-WAM, a compact model with supplied physical state for tracing policy-dynamics interactions. Using 206 Push-T demonstrations and 15 training seeds, we compare data regimes and search configurations. Counterfactual branch training improves short-horizon cost ranking and enlarges the coverage advantage of policy-restarted over warm-started search by 4.8 percentage points; restart wins under both data regimes. Replacing learned trajectory scores with simulator costs improves coverage by 12.2 points while retaining learned proposals. Substituting simulator states in proposal generation alone shows no detected gain. Component diagnostics and a separate door-opening study show why better ranking need not yield better control or outperform imitation. These controlled interventions identify scoring as an effective improvement target in the tested setting and provide a reproducible protocol for diagnosing compact world models.

papers.title: Radial conditions for global compact finite propagation for divergence-form elliptic operators
papers.summary: We study global compact finite propagation (GCFP) for the wave equation $u_{tt}=\operatorname{div}(A(x)\nabla u)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, that is, the property that a disturbance starting in a compact set cannot reach spatial infinity in finite time. For smooth strictly positive matrices $A$ we show that GCFP implies $\int_1^\infty a_*(r)^{-1/2}\,dr=\infty$, where $a_*(r)$ is the minimum over the sphere of radius $r$ of $\langle Aω,ω\rangle$; the proof uses the equivalence of GCFP with completeness of the Riemannian metric $A^{-1}$, of which we prove the necessary direction for the cosine family of the Friedrichs extension. We also prove that the analogous divergence condition with $a^*(r)$, the maximum over the sphere, is sufficient, and that this holds for measurable coefficients $A\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with $A\ge I$. Finally, we construct a locally bounded measurable matrix with $a_*=a^*$ for which GCFP holds although the integral converges, so the necessary condition is not stable under the loss of continuity.

papers.title: A Charged Compact Star Solution for a Conducting Sphere
papers.summary: This paper considers the simplest charged stellar model, namely, a uniform density star with electric charge distributed on its surface. In this model, we treat the uniform density star as a conducting sphere, where all electric charges are uniformly distributed on the surface and represented by a delta function. We obtain an analytical solution for the background metric of the star spacetime and find that the pressure of the perfect fluid inside the star is directed inward (negative pressure) near the inner surface. This is because the repulsive force between surface electric charges requires an inward pressure to maintain equilibrium. However, when the charge becomes too large, the pressure of the ideal fluid at the stellar center gets directed outwards again. This is because the electric field itself is also a part of the stress energy tensor $T_{μν}$, acting as a source of gravity. When the gravitational effect of the electric field dominates, the perfect fluid must provide outward pressure to balance the inward gravitational attraction. On the other hand, we have also studied the axial perturbation in charged spacetimes using the finite difference method. We found that axial Maxwell perturbation and axial gravitational perturbation are coupled in the star spacetime, making it difficult to separate the variables by coordinate transformation. The computational results show that the waveforms of quasinormal modes vary with different charges.

papers.title: GENIE: learned quantum circuits as embedding impurity solvers, and why compactness, not correlation strength, decides when they work
papers.summary: Sample-based quantum diagonalization has been used as an impurity solver in density matrix embedding theory (DMET), but always with fixed-form circuits and without comparison to classical selection at the same subspace size. We introduce GENIE, a DMET impurity solver in which a generative transformer learns the sampling circuit, trained on the quantum-selected configuration interaction energy. On N2, hydrogen chains, water and a hydrogen ring, we compare GENIE at equal determinant budget with classical selected configuration interaction (CIPSI, ASCI, heat-bath CI) and with DMET combined with sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD). GENIE selects: for N2 at 200 determinants it is within a factor of 1.7 of CIPSI and 25 to 1000 times more accurate than the determinants a fixed circuit actually samples, while standard SQD reaches good energies mainly by filling the subspace. GENIE does not beat the best classical selection, and its circuits require fault-tolerant hardware. Its failures are governed by the compactness of the wavefunction relative to the budget, not by correlation strength. A cheap estimate from coupled-cluster amplitudes predicts this compactness. A router built on it never recommended GENIE where it then failed, apart from seed-to-seed variance, and it transferred unchanged to a blind test on new systems. We also identify two benchmarking pitfalls that can create apparent quantum advantages of one to two orders of magnitude.

papers.title: A Compact Formula-Aware Spreadsheet Abstraction for Large Language Models
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to assist spreadsheet users with tasks such as spreadsheet model construction, formula generation, and data analysis, yet their interaction with real-world spreadsheets remains limited by the mismatch between the structure of spreadsheets and the sequential textual representations typically provided to LLMs. We propose a compact formula-aware spreadsheet abstraction that represents large homogeneous ranges through their positions, types, R1C1 formula patterns, and selected boundary values. An efficient algorithm detects and structures these ranges before a textual serialization is supplied to an LLM. The abstraction is provided to the LLM before detailed spreadsheet content is submitted, improving the accuracy and efficiency of spreadsheet processing while reducing token consumption. We evaluate the method on 50 spreadsheet-query cases. The evaluation shows that the abstraction alone was sufficient to answer some queries. When additional spreadsheet content is required, the abstraction reduces the amount of data that must be submitted to the LLM, thereby reducing token consumption. The abstraction layer also improves the reliability and accuracy of spreadsheet processing. We conclude by discussing further techniques for combining spreadsheet static analysis with artificial intelligence to improve the reliability, accuracy, and efficiency of AI assisted spreadsheet tasks.

papers.title: Spectral Haar Binarizer: Compact Boolean Contrast Representations for Hyperspectral Classification
papers.summary: Tsetlin Machines offer an interpretable, hardware-friendly alternative to conventional machine learning models, but applying them to continuous hyperspectral measurements requires converting spectral signals into Boolean representations. Standard binarisation methods typically discretise each spectral band independently, potentially discarding important relationships between neighbouring wavelengths. In this paper, we introduce the Spectral Haar Binarizer (SHB), a contrast-based spectral representation method that constructs Boolean predicates from differences between selected spectral intervals. Inspired by Haar-like contrast features, the method uses an AdaBoost-style selection procedure to obtain a compact set of discriminative spectral predicates. We evaluate SHB on five heterogeneous hyperspectral datasets covering forensic blood detection, agricultural and urban remote sensing, and rainforest tree-species classification. Across binary and multiclass tasks, SHB consistently outperforms standard per-band binarisation strategies and provides the strongest or near-strongest results across classifiers. In binary tasks, TM-SHB achieves the best average performance, while RF-SHB is strongest in multiclass settings. Bayesian and rank-based analyses confirm that SHB's advantage is robust across datasets and not driven by isolated cases. The results show that representing continuous hyperspectral measurements is a central processing step for efficient classification. That contrast-based Boolean features provide an effective bridge between information-rich sensor measurements and compact, logic-based processing.

papers.title: Probing dark sector with decihertz gravitational wave observations of compact binary inspirals in IndIGO-D
papers.summary: We investigate the potential of decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) observations of compact-binary inspirals to probe atomic dark matter (aDM) and its interactions through an ultralight massive dark photon. We consider a scenario in which neutron stars accumulate DM charged under a dark Abelian massive vector mediator, leading to an additional long-range Yukawa interaction between compact objects and associated dipolar radiation. In this framework, the GW waveform acquires characteristic corrections parameterized by the Yukawa coupling strength $α$, the dipole-radiation parameter $γ$, and a parameter related to the mediator mass $μ$. These corrections include a leading $-1$ post-Newtonian dipole contribution and finite-mediator-mass effects. We relate the aDM corrections to existing parameterized tests of general relativity and perform Bayesian parameter-estimation analyses for simulated binary neutron star (BNS) and neutron star-black hole (NSBH) systems incorporating the modified binary inspiral in a proposed space-based decihertz detector, named IndIGO-D. For a GW170817-like BNS with nonzero aDM couplings chosen near current observational bounds, we find that the dark-photon rest energy can be inferred with a $90\%$ credible uncertainty of $O(10^{-20})\,\mathrm{eV}$, conditional on a detectable dark-sector contribution. Analyses with weaker dark-sector interactions $(α\lesssim O(10^{-8}))$ show that the mediator mass remains unconstrained when both the Yukawa coupling and dipole-radiation contribution are negligible, but can be measured even for a negligible Yukawa coupling if the dipole-radiation contribution is sufficiently strong. Our results demonstrate that future decihertz GW observatories can serve as powerful laboratories for testing dark-sector physics and probing dark matter interactions in compact binaries through precision GW measurements.

papers.title: Fock Projections between Gaussian Mixed-Norm Spaces: Full-Range Boundedness and Compactness
papers.summary: The Fock--Bargmann projection \(P_t\) is initially an orthogonal projection on a Gaussian Hilbert space. We characterize the boundedness and compactness of \[ P_t:L_α^{p_1,q_1}\longrightarrow \mathcal F_β^{p_2,q_2} \] and of its associated maximal projection \[ P_t^+:L_α^{p_1,q_1}\longrightarrow L_β^{p_2,q_2} \] for all \(t,α,β>0\) and \(0<p_1,q_1,p_2,q_2\le\infty\). Set \[ Δ(t;α,β):=t^2-2βt+αβ, \qquad d(p,q):=\frac1q-\frac1p. \] For both operators, boundedness holds exactly when \(p_1,q_1\ge1\) and either \(Δ(t;α,β)<0\), or \(Δ(t;α,β)=0\) with \[ q_1\le q_2, \qquad d(p_2,q_2)\le d(p_1,q_1). \] Both operators are compact exactly when \(p_1,q_1\ge1\) and either \(Δ(t;α,β)<0\), or \(Δ(t;α,β)=0\) with both of the above boundary inequalities strict. Thus boundedness forces the source exponents into the Banach range, whereas when \(Δ(t;α,β)<0\), every target exponent is admissible, including quasi-Banach ones. Annular discretization reduces the problem to drifted Gaussian sequence operators, whose comparison with diagonal sequence operators yields the endpoint criteria and quantitative tail estimates. A dilation--multiplier transfer gives corresponding results for Gaussian-twisted Fock operators, including Berezin transforms.

papers.title: Conceptual Design of a Compact Magnetic Spectrometer for Space Radiation Measurement
papers.summary: We present the design of COMIRA, a compact magnetic spectrometer for space radiation measurement. The spectrometer consists of four layers of scintillating fiber trackers, four layers of silicon strip trackers, one threshold Cherenkov counter, two anti-coincidence counters, and a permanent magnet. The detector has an overall dimension of approximately 12x12 cm3 and a geometrical acceptance of ~6.6 cm2sr. Based on combined measurements of charge, velocity, and rigidity (momentum/charge), it enables the simultaneous measurement of the energy spectrum, angular distribution and time evolution of individual radiation components, including electrons, positrons, protons and light nuclei over an energy range from tens of MeV to several GeV. The design can be further optimized depending on the available resources and constraints of the hosting space platform.

papers.title: Two-Fluid Radial Stability of Dark-Matter-Admixed Compact Objects: Dark Compact Planets, Dark White Dwarfs, Dark Neutron Stars, and Dark Oysters
papers.summary: We investigate the equilibrium structure and stability against radial oscillations of a variety of two-fluid compact objects containing ordinary baryonic matter admixed with cold dark matter coupled through the background spacetime. For the ordinary fluid, we employ a QCD equation of state compatible with chiral effective field theory at nuclear densities (supplemented by the BPS and Negele-Vautherin models at extremely low densities) and with perturbative QCD in the high-density regime while also satisfying also current astrophysical data. For the dark fluid, we assume self-interacting fermionic matter with particle masses of $m_f=$ 2, 5, 10, and 100 GeV and two self-interaction strengths of $y=0.1$ and $10^3$. By scanning a large range of central pressures for both fluids, we identify the presence of dark compact planets, dark white dwarfs, dark neutron stars and the so-called dark oysters. Importantly, these objects are not only in two-fluid hydrostatic equilibrium, but they are also stable against two-fluid radial oscillations. We find that the relative representation of each class in the radially stable sample is strongly sensitive to the combinations of $m_f$ and $y$, with some combinations entirely suppressing some of these object classes within the sampled domain while favoring others. In addition to these classes, strong self-repulsion supports stable, dark-matter-dominated branches with compact ordinary-matter cores and extended dark halos, approaching the self-interacting fermion-star limit. Finally, we calculate the gravitational redshift at the ordinary-matter surface, $z_{\rm OM}$, including the contribution of extended dark-matter halos for which we found radially stable configurations with $z_{\rm OM}>2$.

papers.title: Lengths of closed geodesics on random non-compact hyperbolic surfaces
papers.summary: We study the asymptotic distribution of the number of primitive, closed geodesics on Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces with genus $g$ and $n(g)$ cusps, under various growth rates of $n(g)$ as $g\to\infty$. We prove that the limiting distribution is Poisson with parameter depending explicitly on the limit of $n(g)^2/g$. This work is inspired by that of Mirzakhani and Petri's on closed surfaces and Hide and Thomas when $g$ is fixed. Our proof relies on first order expansions for Weil-Petersson moduli space volumes in the $n(g)/g\to 0$ regime. We also obtain some new existence results for small Laplacian eigenvalues.

papers.title: Uniformization of compact Kähler Threefolds of Zero Kodaira Dimension
papers.summary: Given two smooth compact Kähler threefolds $X$ and $Y$ whose universal covers are biholomorphic, we show that $κ(X) = 0$ if and only if $κ(Y) =0$.

papers.title: Kernel-based Interpolatory Methods for Context Compression of Attention Mechanisms
papers.summary: The bottleneck of attention mechanisms, which are the fundamental building block of modern language models, is their quadratic complexity in terms of context size. There has thus been an increasing interest in the compression of the context, also called KV-cache compression. In this article, we consider the problem of compressing the context of attention mechanisms by first formulating it in the Hilbert space associated with its kernel. In this formalism, attention can be represented as the ratio of two linear maps whose interpolant is also the ratio of interpolants, this allows us to consider the interpolation of the linear maps directly. We thus introduce two novel KV-cache compression methods which we call GAIM and Q-DAIM, based on the Generalized Empirical Interpolation Method (GEIM) and the Q-Discrete Empirical Interpolation Method (Q-DEIM), respectively. As the cost of these methods is quadratic in terms of context length, we propose surrogate models based on the Taylor series, the Performer and the Random Fourier Features method which allow the compression to be done in linear time. Finally, we extend this result to the streaming attention setting, providing new methods which allow one to penalize the selection of interpolation nodes based on the previously interpolated context and to update the previous interpolation based on new information. We then provide numerical results on the convergence of the residuals and the output error in future queries and preliminary results on the LongBench-E benchmark showing performance comparable to the state-of-the-art methods. These experiments suggest that the range revealed by our Q-DAIM method could help identify where information is concentrated in the KV cache, thus enabling an efficient compression.

papers.title: Construction and Commissioning of a Compact Xenon Gas Recycling System for a High-Harmonic Generation VUV Frequency Comb
papers.summary: A compact, closed-loop xenon recycling system for application in a High-Harmonic Generation (HHG) Vacuum-UV (VUV) frequency comb laser systems is designed, constructed and commissioned. It consists of three main sections, a low-pressure section (LPS) pre-filtering the gas of particulates, water and hydrocarbons, then a compression station (CS), allowing for a variable pressure of up to 60 bar, and a high-pressure section (HPS) with more filtering, pressure control and monitoring. The system proves to meet all design criteria in gas quality (the sum off all hydrocarbon contaminations up to 120 amu and CO$_{2}$ being below 10$^{-8}$ mbar) and recovery efficiency (>99.8$\%$ for all expected operational cases, neglecting possible geometric gas catcher losses in the HHG laser itself). The operation and results are presented and discussed. Furthermore, the system is compared to the performance of a similar system from which it is derived.

papers.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperkähler Manifolds
papers.summary: We show that all compact hyperkähler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojević and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact Kähler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of multicomplexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.

papers.title: When to Assist and What to Suggest: Joint Gating and Memory-Grounded Hint Generation in One Compact Decoder
papers.summary: Proactive assistants offer short, memory-grounded hints during a conversation, deciding when to assist and what to suggest. Current systems split this between a gate and a larger generator; we evaluate both together on 28,058 decision points. Stage-wise generation scores are oracle-gate ceilings: behind a real gate, end-to-end exact match is 0.2619 against a ceiling of 0.2971, and end-to-end precision is 0.2387, leaving substantial headroom. A gate pays off through precision and compute, whose saving falls from 4.39x with an 8B generator to 1.38x with a 1B one. The memory profile drives hint quality: removing it costs 24.7 exact-match points (rescaled BERTScore 0.57 to 0.35), while retrieval and a larger generator add nothing on exact match. One 1B decoder can do both, gating from an intermediate layer and generating in the same pass. At its final checkpoint it matches or exceeds the two-model pipelines on automatic end-to-end measures with 1.31-1.76x less wall-clock time than the matched 1B pipeline; across three seeds, its deeper exit ties the separate gate. A human evaluation (1,144 ratings over 32 dialogues) supports the memory effect and rates the single model level with the matched 1B pipeline and below the 8B one. Graded metrics and LlamaPIE's native judge track human ratings more closely than exact match, which we report as a strict lower bound.

papers.title: A compact NH$_2$D source without NH$_3$ counterpart in the S187 high-mass star-forming region
papers.summary: Our goal is to investigate a so far only tentatively detected compact NH$_2$D source devoid of a notable NH$_3$ counterpart, located rather close to the luminous IRAS 01202+6133 source (the projected distance is $\lesssim$0.3 pc) in the S187 high-mass star-forming region. A high ammonia deuteration in such an environment is unusual. We performed observations of this area with the 20-m OSO radio telescope in several frequency ranges from $\sim$72 to $\sim$112 GHz. The area was mapped at the lower frequencies while at the higher frequencies only the position of the NH$_2$D emission peak was observed. The data were analyzed using non-LTE modeling. The data confirm a compact NH$_2$D source with a size of $\lesssim$0.2 pc. In addition, emission from about 20 molecules was detected, but only the DCO$^+$(1-0) peak coincides with the NH$_2$D clump. The clump is not associated with any known astronomical source or an NH$_3$ emission peak but the dust continuum map shows an enhancement at approximately the same position. The gas kinetic temperature derived from various indicators is $\sim$20-30 K, which possibly characterizes the surrounding material. The intrinsic NH$_2$D line width ($\sim$0.4 km/s) implies a clump with subsonic or transonic turbulence. The ortho/para NH$_2$D line intensity ratio is consistent with an abundance ratio of 3, expected from the spin statistics. The NH$_2$D/NH$_3$ abundance ratio may be $\sim$1. In general, the data hint at a compact cold gravitationally stable dense core within the warm environment, which may represent pristine material. However this picture still needs a verification with observations at a higher angular resolution.

papers.title: Retrieval Sequencing in a Compact Storage System with Side Access
papers.summary: In a compact storage system with side access, bins are arranged in adjacent vertical stacks. In each retrieval cycle, bins blocking access are lifted to create a temporary tunnel through which a robot extracts one requested bin from the side. The lifted bins are then lowered again, and the energy expenditure of the cycle equals the number of lifted bins. Given a pick list known in advance, we seek a retrieval order that minimizes total energy expenditure. For every number of stacks, we prove that the total energy separates into an instance constant and a pairwise penalty, and that every energy-optimal order is laminar within each stack. For two stacks, we prove that the retrieval sequencing problem is solvable in polynomial time. For three stacks, we give an exact polynomial-time reduction to a merge problem and characterize which merge-problem instances arise from the storage model. We define a recursive class of retrieval orders and construct a polynomial-time dynamic program that minimizes energy expenditure over this class. Finally, we quantify the additional energy savings from batching, which allows several requested bins to be retrieved in one cycle.

papers.title: Compact and Hilbert-Schmidt composition operators on weighted Hardy spaces
papers.summary: Lefèvre, Li, Queffélec, and Rodríguez-Piazza [12] recently characterized the sequences $β$ for which the weighted Hardy space $H^2(β)$ has the same bounded composition operators as the Hardy space $H^2$. We investigate the analogous questions for the compactness and the $p$-Schatten classes: for which sequences $β$ does the space $H^2(β)$ have the same compact or $p$-Schatten class composition operators as $H^2$?

papers.title: Locally unital $C^*$-algebras and limitations of seminorm criteria for compact operators
papers.summary: We study the problem of geometric characterization of Banach-compact and $\mathcal A$-compact operators on Hilbert $C^*$-modules in terms of uniform structures generated by seminorms. Previously, such a criterion for $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators was obtained by Troitsky for countably generated range modules with a suitable system of seminorms. Using locally unital $C^*$-algebras as modules over themselves, we establish fundamental limitations of such characterizations. Namely, we show that for nonunital locally unital $C^*$-algebras not only does Troitsky's criterion fail to extend, but, more generally, no system of seminorms can characterize $\mathcal A$-precompactness by total boundedness, nor Banach-compactness of bounded operators or $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators by total boundedness of the images of the unit ball. Moreover, the same statement holds for Hilbert $C^*$-modules $\mathcal N$ whenever the algebra $\mathbf K(\mathcal N)$ of $\mathcal A$-compact operators is locally unital and nonunital. We also study Troitsky-type systems of seminorms and their relation to $\mathcal A$-precompactness. We prove that every $\mathcal A$-precompact subset is totally bounded with respect to the strongest of such structures. Consequently, for Hilbert $C^*$-modules admitting a standard frame, all the corresponding notions of total boundedness coincide.

papers.title: Lev-3B: A Data Recipe for Compact Probabilistic Log Decision Models
papers.summary: Many log-analysis tasks involve choosing among known options, such as detecting anomalous sessions or identifying attack techniques, and benefit from calibrated probabilities. We present Lev-3B, an open 3B-parameter decision model built on Granite-4.1-3B-Base with a shared pointer readout, and study its training recipe. The recipe has two key parts. First, training follows a curriculum: the model learns bounded natural-language decisions, using no log data, before it sees any logs. Second, the log stage mixes the target tasks with general log data spanning 35 auxiliary tasks unrelated to either evaluation task. We evaluate one shared checkpoint on sources seen in training and on sources excluded from training, calibration and model selection. The two-stage recipe transfers substantially better than training on log data alone. Adding general log data improves performance on excluded sources.
