We will release our code and model weights at https://github.com/JianzeLi-114/FrameLite .

papers.title: Observational evidence of black hole event horizon from ultra-compact X-ray binaries
papers.summary: The event horizon is the most crucial feature that distinguishes black hole (BH) from all other objects in the universe. However, since no radiation can escape from the event horizon, its direct observational evidence remains lacking. Although both are compact objects, the event horizon leads to differences in the radiative behavior between black hole and neutron star (NS) X-ray binaries. Historically efforts to probe the existence of event horizons revealed that the BH X-ray binaries are fainter than NSs with similar orbital periods in their quiescent states. Here, we use a special class of X-ray binaries namely the ultra-compact X-ray binaries (UCXBs), to reveal the existence of the event horizon near stellar-mass black holes. In short-period UCXBs, gravitational radiation dominates the orbital angular momentum loss, allowing us to accurately determine their accretion rates. Based on five UCXBs with orbital periods shorter than 40 min, located in globular clusters, and identified accretors (NS or BH), we obtained their accretion rates. Combining their accretion rates and X-ray luminosities, we calculated the X-ray radiative efficiencies of NS and BH. The radiative efficiency of BH is about two to three orders of magnitude lower than that of NS systems, indicating the accretion energy is swallowed by the BH, thereby indirectly probe the presence of the event horizon.

papers.title: Box-WAM: Box Trajectories as Compact State Representations for World Action Models
papers.summary: World action models (WAMs) are a category of policy models that ex- plicitly predict both actions and future world states. They have been shown to outperform action-only models across various robotic manipulation tasks. How- ever, representing the future with full-frame video prediction can be computation- ally expensive during both training and inference. This raises a central question: what compact state representation preserves the planning and supervision bene- fits of future prediction? In this paper, we propose BoxWAM, which replaces dense future frames with oriented bounding box trajectories of task-relevant ob- jects. By explicitly imagining object-centric future motion, our method provides a lightweight prediction target that captures the key physical changes induced by robot actions. We show that box trajectory prediction substantially reduces com- putational cost while improving action prediction performance, suggesting that object-centric compact states can serve as an efficient alternative to video-based world action modeling for robotic manipulation. Result videos can be found on https://box-wam.github.io

papers.title: Compactness of Cone Yang-Mills Connections
papers.summary: We consider the cone Yang-Mills functional recently introduced by Tseng and Zhou. This functional generalizes the Yang-Mills functional by coupling it to a closed 2-form which can represent a geometric structure of interest, e.g. a symplectic form or Ricci form. While the perspective of dimensional reduction is not always possible, we show that a cone Yang-Mills field is always locally the dimensional reduction of a pure Yang-Mills field. We then prove a monotonicity formula and use the dimensional reduction framework to prove an $ε$-regularity theorem in two ways. Finally, we prove a compactness theorem for sequences of cone Yang-Mills connections with bounded action and $L^p$-bounded Higgs fields. Away from a singular set of codimension at least 4 and after suitable bundle identifications, the sequence subconverges in the $C^\infty_{\operatorname{loc}}$-topology.

papers.title: Finiteness of Fuchsian equations with unitarizable monodromy on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.summary: We prove that, on any compact Riemann surface, there are only finitely many meromorphic projective connections with prescribed singular points and real exponent differences whose projective monodromy is unitarizable. We also establish properness and growth estimates for holonomy, including a relative version for smooth marked families, and derive finiteness results for spherical conical metrics and ramification divisors of stable extensions.

papers.title: Audit Before You Distill: A Controlled Workflow for Reasoning Transfer into Compact Medical Language Models
papers.summary: Teacher rationales can help a smaller model answer health professions questions, but they can also reinforce errors. We examined when they help and how this evidence can guide training using Brazilian Portuguese questions from medical and multiprofessional residency examinations. First, we measured how a teacher rationale changed the student's probability of selecting the correct answer and compared this effect with rationales drawn from other questions. The complete rationale increased this probability by 21~p.p. when the teacher was correct and decreased it by 14~p.p. when the teacher was wrong. By intervening on the reasoning content, we showed that shuffled rationales did not produce the same pattern. Guided by this result, we trained only with rationales attached to correct teacher answers and compared answer-only training, step-by-step distillation, and our proposed Distill-SFT method. Distill-SFT showed a modest advantage over step-by-step distillation on previously missed questions under reasoning, while using fewer training instances by combining the answer and rationale into a single target. We also investigated catastrophic forgetting using the out-of-domain ENEM dataset. Answer-only training reduced reasoning accuracy by 12~p.p. relative to baseline, compared with approximately 4~p.p. for either rationale-based training method. Together, these findings support a workflow that audits rationale content before distillation, verifies teacher answers before supervision, and trains compact models efficiently for health professions question answering.

papers.title: Pointwise Ergodic Theorems Along Reiter Sequences on Locally Compact Groups
papers.summary: Let $G$ be a locally compact, second countable group admitting a Reiter sequence, and suppose that $G$ acts on a von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ equipped with a semifinite trace $τ$ via trace-preserving automorphisms. In this paper, we prove a maximal inequality for ergodic averages along such Reiter sequences. Our approach relies on approximating the Reiter sequence by a linear combination of characteristic functions of Følner sequences using the layer-cake representation. Furthermore, we establish the bilateral almost uniform convergence of these ergodic averages. As an application, we deduce a non-commutative Wiener-Wintner type theorem along Reiter sequences.

papers.title: Order convergence in ordered vector spaces: compactness, atoms, pervasiveness, and ice cream spaces
papers.summary: We study order convergence in ordered vector spaces that are not necessarily lattices. In this setting, we consider two generalizations of order convergence on vector lattices, a directed and an undirected variant. We show that these notions agree for the class of pervasive spaces and extend several results concerning atomicity and order convergence in vector lattices to this class. In particular, we prove that a pervasive JB-algebra is associative, which strengthens a result of Sherman for C*-algebras. We also establish a number of new characterizations of pervasive spaces. Additionally, we systematically study a class of order unit spaces associated to Banach spaces, called ice cream spaces. We provide descriptions of both directed and undirected order convergences in these spaces, yielding examples where the two notions differ. We also consider other order-theoretic aspects of ice cream spaces, such as atoms and lattice operations, relating them to the geometry of the underlying Banach spaces. We demonstrate that ice cream spaces exhibit behavior very different from vector lattices and can serve as a rich source of counterexamples in the theory of ordered vector spaces.

papers.title: BARTER: Compact Dynamic Sparse Training with Standard Dense Kernels
papers.summary: Dynamic sparse training (DST) aims to reduce training costs while maintaining accuracy. Existing DST methods mask out parameters but keep matrix dimensions unchanged. Training speedups therefore depend on specialized support, such as sparse kernels. We introduce BARTER, a structured DST framework that reduces training cost using standard dense kernels by keeping training tensors physically compact while dynamically reallocating capacity across layers. Unlike existing works that require computing gradients for all parameters, BARTER instead uses statistics collected only from active units during ordinary backpropagation to prune and clone attention heads and feed-forward channels under separate fixed global budgets. At each topology update, it resizes the affected parameter tensors and remaps their optimizer states, so subsequent training steps operate directly on the compact model. Training and fine-tuning experiments with Transformer-based vision models on two image classification benchmarks at densities from $0.1$ to $0.7$ show competitive Top-1 accuracy relative to full-tensor DST baselines. On an NVIDIA L40, BARTER achieves speedups of up to $6.29\times$ in measured training segments and reduces peak allocated GPU memory by up to $81.3\%$ relative to these implementations. An iPhone 13 Pro Max training benchmark additionally shows a $2.78\times$ speedup over the full-tensor DST baseline.

papers.title: Hashrope: A Persistent Data Structure for Mechanisms of LLM Context Management
papers.summary: Serving stacks for large language models manage context through four recurring mechanisms: incremental edits to a growing context, branching and snapshotting for tree search, identification of reusable prefixes for KV-cache reuse, and encoding of repeated segments. Each mechanism is served today by a different specialist structure. We show that all four reduce to a single persistent weight-balanced rope whose every node carries a polynomial hash of its subtree over a Mersenne prime, so that the structure supports logarithmic edits and logarithmic verified content-identity queries at the same time. We validate each mechanism with pre-registered, replicated experiments, then compare against a deployed specialist per mechanism: the Ropey editing library, a faithful PagedAttention copy-on-write block table, and the vendored SGLang radix matcher. On workloads that interleave edits with identity queries, Hashrope is net-superior to Ropey by a factor that grows without bound (369.7x at one million characters). Against the radix matcher on a live vLLM stack serving Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M on four A100 GPUs, Hashrope identifies a one-million-token shared prefix exactly and 1.20x faster, at a context length the dense engine cannot even prefill.

papers.title: A chain theorem for planar PM-compact bricks
papers.summary: A connected graph $G$ is matching covered if it contains at least one edge and every edge belongs to some perfect matching of $G$. A matching covered graph is a brick if it is 3-connected and after removing any two vertices, the resulting graph has a perfect matching. Bricks are the building blocks of matching covered graphs. A brick $G$ is extremal if the incidence vectors of all perfect matchings are linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$. Zhou et al. [On planar extremal nonsolid bricks, J. Graph Theory, 2026] proved that for every planar extremal brick $G$, there exists a sequence of planar extremal bricks $G_0,G_1,\dots,G_n$ such that the underlying graph of $G_n$ is an odd wheel, $G_0=G$, and each $G_i$ $(0\leq i < n)$ has a triangle $T_i$ such that $G_i/T_i = G_{i+1}$, where $G_i/T_i$ means contracting the triangle $T_i$ into a single vertex. In this paper, the result of Zhou et al. is generalized to planar PM-compact bricks, a larger class of bricks including extremal bricks. We present a chain theorem for planar PM-compact bricks: for every planar PM-compact brick $G$, there exists a sequence of planar PM-compact bricks $G_0,G_1,\dots,G_n$ such that the underlying graph of $G_n$ is an odd wheel, $G_0=G$, and each $G_i$ $(0\leq i < n)$ contains a triangle $T_i$ such that $G_i/T_i = G_{i+1}$.

papers.title: Extended-range percolation on lattices with cubic and non-compact neighborhoods in three dimensions
papers.summary: Using MC simulations based on an efficient single-cluster growth algorithm, we investigate two types of three-dimensional extended-range percolation models, namely cubic and complex (non-compact) neighborhoods. We obtain high-precision percolation thresholds $p_c$ for approximately 100 distinct structures and further explore the relationship between these thresholds and the topology of the lattices, which includes the total coordination number $z$, the number of sites $z_i$ and these sites' distance to the central site $r_i$ of the given neighborhood in the $i$th coordination zone. Both bond and site percolation are analyzed for cubic neighborhoods on the SC lattice. For bond percolation, the asymptotic value of $zp_c$ tends to Bethe-lattice behavior ($zp_c\sim1$), and finite-$z$ correction is found to be consistent with $zp_{c}-1\sim a_{1}z^{-x}$, where $x=(d-1)/d$. For site percolation, the value of $zp_c$ varies non-monotonically, exhibiting an initial increase followed by a decrease with the coordination number $z$. Linear fitting leads to $zp_c\sim2.5987(1)$ for large $z$, predicting a value of continuum percolation threshold of aligned cubes $η_c=0.324838(12)$ using $zp_c=2^{d}η_c$. We then examine site percolation for non-compact neighborhoods extending to the fifth coordination zone on SC, FCC, and BCC lattices. Through a comparison of the three indices of $z$, $ξ=\sum_iz_ir_i^2/i$, and $ζ=\sum_iz_ir_i$, we find that $ζ$ is effective in removing the degeneracy. The results obtained show power-law dependence $p_c\propto(ζ/K)^{-γ}$ with $γ_{\mathrm{SC}}^ζ=0.703(12)$, $γ_{\mathrm{FCC}}^ζ=0.728(10)$, and $γ_{\mathrm{BCC}}^ζ=0.699(12)$ for SC, FCC, and BCC lattices, and $p_c\proptoζ^{-γ}$ with $γ^ζ=0.719(9)$ independent of the underlying lattice. The number $K$ indicates lattice connectivity.

papers.title: Boundary-induced corrections to the response of an Unruh-DeWitt detector outside a compact star with Robin surface conditions
papers.summary: We formulate the finite-time response problem for a radially accelerated Unruh--DeWitt detector coupled to a real massless scalar field outside a static, spherically symmetric, horizonless compact star. The stellar exterior is described by the Schwarzschild geometry, while unresolved field--surface interactions are represented by a local Robin condition at the stellar radius. After reducing the Klein--Gordon equation to a half-line Schrödinger problem, we identify a sufficiently stable branch of the Robin family from positivity of the radial operator, construct delta-normalized continuum modes, and define the static ground state with respect to Schwarzschild time. We derive a mode-amplitude representation of the smoothly switched detector response that avoids a direct numerical treatment of the coincidence singularity of the Wightman distribution. We obtain a radially aligned trajectory of constant signed proper acceleration in terms of the rapidity measured by static observers. The resulting formulation separates the effects of compactness, surface condition, closest approach, detector gap, and interaction duration. We also state the flat-space, Dirichlet, static-detector, low-frequency, large-distance, and long-interaction limits required to validate a numerical implementation. The framework provides a controlled extension of detector studies with static reflective compact objects to finite-time moving probes.

papers.title: A note on the Chern-Yamabe flow on compact Hermitian manifolds with negative Gauduchon degree
papers.summary: In this note, we prove that on a compact Hermitian manifold with negative Gauduchon degree, the Chern-Yamabe flow introduced in our recent work [13] converges to the solution of prescribed Chern scalar curvature problem, provided that the candidate curvature function is nonpositive and not identically zero.

papers.title: Exponential Green energies, quantization, and minimizers on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.summary: We study the exponential Green energies associated with a finite point configuration on a Riemann surface. We focus on studying optimal or close-to-optimal configurations, and show that they must be well-spread out on the surface. We study in particular the round sphere and obtain values for the minimal Green energy of a configuration. The first version of this paper was written with the help of ChatGPT.

papers.title: Compactness and essential norms for two-weight fractional Riesz transforms on curves
papers.summary: We prove a compact two-weight $T1$ theorem for the $α$-fractional Riesz vector, $0\leqα<n$, when one measure is supported on a compact regular $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ curve $Γ$. The measures may have common point masses. Under the global boundedness assumptions, we give a two-sided estimate for the essential norm in terms of Muckenhoupt and testing constants computed after restricting both measures to small cubes. Compactness is equivalent to the uniform vanishing of these local bounds as the cube side length tends to zero. The smooth truncations have a unique weak operator limit and converge in operator norm in the compact case. For arclength measure and distance power weights, we determine the compactness ranges for Green gradients on bounded tubes and for Newtonian gradients and Biot--Savart fields on the whole space. The whole-space operators in these ranges are compact but are not Hilbert--Schmidt. When $α=n-1$ and both measures have positive continuous arclength densities $a,b$ on the same closed curve, we obtain the exact essential norm $πc_{n-1,n}\max_Γ\sqrt{ab}$.

papers.title: Uniform Green packing on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.summary: We extend the packing results of Etayo, Hedenmalm, and Ortega-Cerda for complex tori to arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces. The construction uses two different approaches, one based on complex geometry of line bundles, and the other on Laplace designs. Both approaches give the same basic existence of close-to-optimal point configurations on the given surface. This version was written with the help of ChatGPT.

papers.title: Global $C^{2,α}$ estimate for complex Monge--Ampère equations on compact Kähler manifolds
papers.summary: In this paper, we prove a global $C^{2,α}$ estimate for the complex Monge--Ampère equation with a positive $C^α$ right-hand side on a compact Kähler manifold.

papers.title: Physics-informed random neural architectures on compact boundaryless multiply connected manifolds for random-operator models in machine learning and uncertainty quantification
papers.summary: We introduce stochastic physics-informed neural networks (SPINNs) for stochastic boundary-value problems (SBVPs) with random operators. The method enforces physics through a structural probabilistic coupling: a common Gaussian stochastic germ drives both the SBVP random operator and a manifold-based stochastic neural architecture. The stochastic neural network is non-feedforward and intrinsically random. A latent Gaussian field and an inhomogeneous Poisson point process on a compact, boundaryless, multiply connected manifold generate random neuron locations, geodesically local sparse connectivity, and a sparse random weight matrix, all governed by a low-dimensional hyperparameter. For deterministic inputs, the network output is random and can represent non-Gaussian random operators. Training is performed in observation space: SBVP simulations produce random observables, while the SNN defines a predictive conditional probability density function. The supervised objective combines data fidelity, through negative log-likelihood, with a cross-entropy alignment term relative to the SBVP-induced conditional distribution. The resulting target is a convex mixture of observation-induced and SBVP-induced distributions, with a dimensionless parameter controlling robustness to model--data mismatch. The shared stochastic germ yields common-random-numbers Monte Carlo estimators and reduced-variance gradients. The method uses only evaluations of the SBVP solution mapping, without differentiating or modifying it, and avoids PDE-residual or boundary-penalty losses. A stochastic elliptic problem on a periodic cylindrical surface illustrates the approach in SBVP-consistent and SBVP-misspecified regimes. A generalized-posterior formulation is also outlined for hyperparameter inference and posterior averaging without per-query reoptimization.

papers.title: The CR Nirenberg Problem, Part I: Blow-up Analysis and Compactness
papers.summary: We establish a priori estimates and compactness results for positive solutions of the CR Nirenberg problem under natural weighted flatness conditions. The proofs combine refined blow-up analysis, Pohozaev identities, and the complete classification of positive entire solutions to the critical CR Yamabe equation recently obtained by Li--Liu--Ma \cite{LLM2026} and Li \cite{L2026}. Existence and degree results are established in our subsequent paper \cite{QTWPartII}.

papers.title: Training a Compact, Strong, and Realistic Text-to-Speech Model
papers.summary: Text-to-speech (TTS) systems are conventionally optimized for intelligibility and speaker similarity. However, neither objective captures the prosodic detail that distinguishes human performances from synthetic speech, leaving a realism gap that larger models and higher-quality data can narrow but not close. In the absence of an objective that directly targets this gap, realism remains a persistent challenge in TTS. We present Audio8-TTS, a compact 0.6B-parameter model for zero-shot voice cloning that achieves state-of-the-art performance in intelligibility and speaker similarity, with particularly strong results in perceptual naturalness. To align the training signal with human perception rather than signal-level fidelity, we construct a quality ladder from widely used open-source TTS systems and train a realism critic to assess generated speech against matched human recordings of the same sentences. An identity-erasure objective discourages the critic from relying on generator fingerprints. We train the model in three stages: multilingual supervised fine-tuning; group relative policy optimization (GRPO) with word error rate (WER) and speaker similarity (SIM) rewards; and GRPO guided by the realism critic. The final stage improves perceived prosodic naturalness and speaker similarity while preserving WER performance.

papers.title: LightVAE: Towards Compact and Efficient Video Autoencoders
papers.summary: Latent diffusion models enable high-quality video generation, but video VAE encoding and decoding remain computationally expensive. Existing methods use stage-specific lightweight operators, yet either constrain spatial and temporal computation jointly or remove temporal computation altogether, without distinguishing their compression sensitivities in pretrained Conv3D. To address these limitations, we present LightVAE, a compression framework that exploits redundancy in temporal modeling and network depth. LightVAE exactly reparameterizes eligible causal Conv3D layers into an aggregate spatial response and a difference-driven temporal correction. Based on their distinct compression sensitivities, temporal low-rank compression (TLR) keeps the aggregate spatial kernel dense and applies layer-specific low-rank approximation only to the temporal correction. An algebraically equivalent folded implementation converts the arithmetic savings into practical acceleration. LightVAE further uses width-preserving block pruning to reduce depth and probe-guided feature alignment, guided by feedback from a frozen teacher suffix, to recover quality after compression. The framework also extends to video encoders. Across three video VAE backbones and two GPU platforms, LightVAE consistently accelerates decoding. For the Wan VAE family, it achieves up to $2.24\times$ and $1.11\times$ the decoding throughput of state-of-the-art efficient VAE decoders on NVIDIA H100 and RTX~5090, respectively, with higher DAVIS PSNR and lower LPIPS. On MiniMax-H3, it achieves up to $2.97\times$ the original decoding throughput while retaining 99.51\% of the original model's overall VBench-2.0 score. Our code is available at https://github.com/ModelTC/LightVAE.

papers.title: SpikCTU: A Compact Spiking Network with Adaptive Recurrent Computation for Speech Command Recognition
papers.summary: Spiking Neural Networks offer event-driven, energy-efficient computation for speech command recognition, yet most existing methods follow fixed computation paths, allocating redundant computation to easy samples while providing limited insight into how evidence evolves during inference. To address these challenges, we introduce SpikCTU, a compact spiking network with adaptive recurrent computation for speech command recognition. Specifically, a hybrid spiking embedding module preserves continuous input information alongside spike features to construct a fixed temporal memory. A shared Continuous Thinking Unit (CTU) repeatedly reads this memory using keys derived from spikes and continuous values, and updates a binary recurrent state with lightweight stage adapters. Furthermore, combining a fixed base prediction with accumulated corrections at each step enables learned aggregation over all steps or confidence-based early exit using only the predictions available so far. Experiments on three speech command recognition benchmarks show that SpikCTU achieves competitive accuracy with only 0.16--0.17M parameters, and the early exit strategy can substantially further reduce computational cost without compromising accuracy. In addition, trajectory and attention analyses reveal that recurrent steps enable error correction and progressively refine predictions. Code is available at https://github.com/Rivflyyy/spikctu.

papers.title: Compact localization and co-sobriety of Smyth power spaces
papers.summary: We establish a compact-localization theorem for finite iterates of the Smyth power space. Successive union maps assign to every finite-level Smyth object a canonical least compact saturated carrier in the original space, and co-sobriety at each positive finite level is equivalent to co-sobriety of the corresponding iterates over all compact saturated carriers. Consequently, if every compact saturated subspace of a $T_0$-space $X$ is stably compact---in particular, if every such subspace is Hausdorff---then $\PS^n(X)$ is co-sober for every finite $n\geq 1$. This applies to every $k_1$-Hausdorff space and hence to every Hausdorff or metrizable space. For the first iterate, we also give a direct full-Vietoris argument, independent of stable compactness, which shows that each $k$-irreducible compact saturated family is generated by its union.

papers.title: Flat and Ghost dimensions in tensor triangulated categories with a compact tilting generator
papers.summary: Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a tensor triangulated category with a compact tilting generator $M$ and abelian heart $\mathcal{H}_M = M^{\bot_{\neq0}}$. We define a triangulated flat dimension $\mathrm{flatdim}_{\mathcal{T}}X$ for $X\in\mathcal{T}$, and give criteria in terms of tensor vanishing and resolutions by the class of pure quotients of $\mathrm{Add}(M)$. We further introduce $M$-ghost length and $M$-ghost dimension, and show that the global dimension of $\mathcal{H}_M$ controls the $M$-ghost length of all objects in $\mathcal{T}$, and that the $M$-ghost dimension of $\mathcal{T}$ coincides with the weak global dimension of $\mathcal{H}_M$ and the supremum of $\mathrm{flatdim}_{\mathcal{T}}X+\mathrm{inf}X$ of bounded objects, and the relative triangulated dimension of $\mathcal{T}^c$ with respect to $\mathrm{add}(M)$. This extends the classical Hovey-Lockridge theorem, which is recovered for derived categories of rings.

papers.title: Compact Quasi-Metric Spaces Are Expand-Contract Plastic
papers.summary: On a totally bounded metric space every non-contractive self-map is an isometry. For quasi-metric spaces, taken T_1 throughout, this fails: Zavarzina gave a hereditarily precompact counterexample and asked whether bijectivity restores rigidity; the toll spiral shows that it does not. We prove that compactness does: every compact quasi-metric space is expand-contract plastic, that is, each of its bijective non-contractive self-maps is an isometry. Countable compactness suffices, as does compactness of the conjugate topology. Bijectivity cannot be dropped: a compact, hereditarily precompact quasi-metric on the natural numbers makes the shift non-contractive and not an isometry. For arbitrary non-contractive self-maps we prove rigidity when the space is hereditarily precompact and its conjugate topology is sequentially compact, in particular when it is hereditarily precompact and Yoneda complete; neither hypothesis can be dropped. In both theorems the T_1 axiom can be weakened to R_0, with hereditary precompactness read sequentially, but not to T_0: we construct a T_0 space with all the remaining hypotheses of both theorems, carrying a bijective non-contractive self-map that is not an isometry. Under R_0 the two-sided case reduces to the metric theorem; the one-sided theorems do not, and plasticity does not pass to the symmetrization even for compact spaces. In finite dimension the unit ball of a T_1 asymmetric normed space, forward or symmetric, and its sphere are rigid for every non-contractive self-map; without T_1 the forward ball need not be; in infinite dimension the symmetric ball and sphere are not plastic in general, and the forward versions carry the quasi-metric form of the unit-ball question of Cascales, Kadets, Orihuela and Wingler, which is posed. The two theorems are machine-checked in Lean, and so are the counterexamples, apart from a few statements listed at the end.

papers.title: Compact lcK manifolds with Gauduchon parallel vector fields
papers.summary:
We prove that on a compact locally conformally Kähler manifold, the existence of a non-trivial parallel vector field with respect to a Gauduchon connection $
abla^t$, for $t
e  rac{1}{3}$, forces the metric to be either Vaisman (for $t=-1$), globally conformally Kähler (for $t=1$), or Kähler for all other values of $t$. As a consequence, we characterize compact Vaisman manifolds in terms of their Bismut holonomy group. Moreover, we show that in complex dimension two, the existence of a non-trivial $
abla^ rac{1}{3}$-parallel vector field forces the metric to be globally conformally Kähler.

papers.title: AMLworld-Compact: Importance-Weighted Downsampling for Cost-Effective LLM Evaluation and Error Diagnosis
papers.summary: Evaluating large language models (LLMs) on AMLworld's smallest test splits is costly because each of over a million targets requires a separate graph prompt. Sampling reduces this cost, but small balanced subsets change unweighted precision and F1. We introduce AMLworld-Compact, an evaluation set that retains every illicit test transaction and samples benign transactions from supervised-score strata. Its HT-Coreset protocol reduces evaluation targets by 271x and 611x on HI-Small and LI-Small. Horvitz-Thompson weights give unbiased full-test confusion-count estimates for fixed predictions; recall is exact, while precision and F1 are ratio estimates. In a held-out study using Graph Feature Preprocessor (GFP) features, one boosted-tree family defines strata for evaluating the other over 500 draws per configuration. At the released sizes, F1 RMSE is 0.00-2.58 percentage points versus 4.44-7.41 for uniform sampling with HT weights; conservative intervals remain broad. Under the evaluated graph prompts, seven open-weight LLMs have weighted precision near the predict-all-illicit baseline. In an outcome-stratified audit of 1,000 HI-Small few-shot outputs from one run per model, lexical checks pass for 84.5% of correct and 56.2% of incorrect binary verdicts, so these markers do not establish correctness. We release the evaluation sets, construction code, and audit tools at https://huggingface.co/datasets/typhoon-ai/AMLworldCompactEval and https://github.com/nat-nischw/AMLworld-Compact.

papers.title: Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint linear relations with an application to elliptic boundary value problems
papers.summary: We establish a spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint linear relations on a Hilbert space. The proof relies on the Arens decomposition of a closed linear relation into an operator part and a purely multivalued part, reducing the problem directly to the classical spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators. No finite-dimensionality condition is imposed on the multivalued part. We also prove a finiterank approximation theorem for compact bounded linear relations and a Fredholm alternative for compact self-adjoint linear relations. As an application, we employ the theory of boundary triples to show that the inverse of the Neumann Laplacian on a bounded domain is a compact self-adjoint linear relation. The abstract spectral theorem then recovers the classical eigenfunction expansion of solutions to the Neumann problem: an L2-convergent series in terms of the non-constant Neumann eigenfunctions together with an arbitrary additive constant. The framework extends naturally to general elliptic boundary value problems with finite-dimensional kernel.

papers.title: Second quantization and compactness of induced Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups
papers.summary: We characterize compactness of the Hilbert-Schmidt semigroups induced by finite-mode Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful normal invariant state. A unitary second-quantization representation for every $ s $-embedding shows that compactness at one positive time, compact resolvent, drift stability, and uniqueness of the normal invariant state are equivalent. These conditions imply immediate trace-class membership for all embeddings. We derive exact trace-norm and Hilbert-Schmidt norm formulas, an embedding-independent trace identity, and the generator spectrum with algebraic multiplicities. Examples show that compactness does not require the existence of a spectral gap and that a spectral gap need not imply compactness when the invariant state is not unique.

papers.title: Compact Quantitative Equational Theories as Monad Restrictions
papers.summary: Proofs in quantitative algebra are, generally, infinite objects due to the presence of infinitary rules in the deductive apparatus. A quantitative equational theory is called compact if all its consequences are derivable by means of finite proofs, that is, proofs not using any instances of the infinitary rules. This definition is purely logical. In this work we give an equivalent, but categorical, characterisation based on the notion of monad restriction.

papers.title: Detailed study of HD 219134: a benchmark K-dwarf with a compact planetary system
papers.summary: Space missions such as CoRoT, Kepler, and TESS have transformed asteroseismology and its synergies with exoplanet science. We revisit the nearby K-dwarf HD 219134 to investigate the tension between asteroseismic and interferometric radii, update its fundamental parameters, and reconstruct the rotational, magnetic, and atmospheric evolution of the system. We combine forward asteroseismic modeling with seismic inversions to assess systematics from non-seismic constraints, radius measurements, and surface modeling. The revised stellar properties are then used for rotational evolution, stellar-wind, and high-energy irradiation calculations. Seismic inversions rule out the most recent interferometric radius, while the asteroseismic and spectroscopic results are compatible with the 2019 interferometric measurement. We obtain $M=0.779\pm0.015_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.006_\mathrm{(sys)}\ M_\odot$, $R=0.753\pm0.005_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.002_\mathrm{(sys)}\ R_\odot$, and an age of $8.92\pm0.89_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.19_\mathrm{(sys)}$ Gyr. These systematics include only non-seismic constraints; literature combined uncertainties from physical inputs and surface effects are $0.007M_\odot$, $0.002R_\odot$, and $0.81$ Gyr. Rotational and wind modelling shows that standard magnetic braking is broadly compatible with the present-day rotation and angular-momentum loss. Weakened braking gives a closer match but challenges standard wind-loss scalings. The inferred X-ray history suggests early stripping of the innermost planets, while the outer planets likely retained part of their primordial envelopes; HD 219134d experienced only moderate erosion. The apparent radius discrepancy likely reflects underestimated uncertainties in previous interferometric analyses rather than an astrophysical inconsistency. We advocate adopting the asteroseismic radius, which is robust to modeling assumptions and optimisation strategies.

papers.title: Generalized Gauduchon metrics on compact complex spaces
papers.summary: Let $X$ be an irreducible reduced compact complex space of dimension $n$, and let $ω$ be a Hermitian metric on $X$. For each $1\le k\le n-1$, we prove that there exist a constant $c_k$ and a smooth positive function $ρ$ on $X_{\mathrm{reg}}$ such that $\ii\partial\bar\partial(ρω^k)\wedgeω^{n-k-1}=c_kρω^n$. The function $ρ$ is bounded above and bounded away from zero. The constant $c_k$ is unique, and $ρ$ is unique up to a positive multiple among bounded smooth positive solutions. We also prove that the full sign set $\{-1,0,1\}$ of the generalized Gauduchon constants $c_k$ on a compact complex manifold is preserved by finite sequences of blow-ups with smooth centers.

papers.title: Compact Mean Curvature Flows from Non-Compact Initial Data
papers.summary: We construct compact, embedded solutions to the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ that arise from various non-compact initial data and exist for a finite time.

papers.title: A Compact Weight-Space Integer Programming Formulation for Balanced Minimum Evolution
papers.summary: Balanced Minimum Evolution (BME) reconstructs an unrooted binary phylogenetic tree from a distance matrix $D$ by minimizing the length $\sum_{i<j}D_{ij}w_{ij}$, which is linear in the weights $w_{ij}=2^{-d_T{ij}}$. We study the formulation of BME in these $\binom{n}{2}$ weight variables. Theoretical results. (i) For a fixed topology $T$, the Kraft equalities, the cut equalities $\{W[S]=\tfrac12\}$ of $T$, and the single convex constraint $\sum w_{ij} \log_2 w_{ij} \leq \tfrac{3}{2}-n$ admit exactly one point, the tree's weight vector. (ii) For every tree and every bipartition, the cut value $W_T[S]$ lies in $\{\tfrac{1}{2}\} \cup \{\tfrac{3}{4}\} \cup [\tfrac{7}{8}, \infty)$; the value $\tfrac{3}{4}$ is attained exactly by the $2(n-3)$ bipartitions created by one nearest-neighbour interchange; and the number of bipartitions with $W_T[S]\le1$ is $2n^2-10n+15$ for every binary topology. (iii) The crossing graph of nontrivial bipartitions has an edge clique cover with $O(n^4)$ cliques, and every edge clique cover needs $Ω(n^2)$. (iv) The necessary conditions of Catanzaro et al. for a path-length matrix, without the four-point condition, are sufficient for $n \leq 11$ and first fail at $n=12$. Computational results. A compact branch-and-bound solver built on these results, which commits and forbids splits and imposes the convex constraint exactly, certifies optimality on benchmark instances with up to $n=20$ taxa within an hour. It is faster than the distance-indexed model of Catanzaro et al. on two of these instances and slower on the others; that model, whose root bound is tighter, certifies 13 of 14 benchmark instances with $n \leq 30$ within an hour in every seed. Although the compact solver does not improve on the computational state of the art overall, we explain why, and we discuss the open problems that our results raise.

papers.title: An exact Delaunay flux identity for compact equilibria in the liquid drop model
papers.summary: We revisit the construction of compact liquid drop equilibria from Delaunay unduloids in [Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 249 (2025), Paper No. 74]. We evaluate exactly the coefficient arising in the final solvability condition of the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction, identifying it as the product of the axial period and the normalised Delaunay flux. Using this identity and the monotonicity of the period, we establish the conjectured positivity of the coefficient and prove that its product with the period strictly increases with the neck radius. We also derive an exact relation between the volume and the surface area of one period and prove that both strictly decrease with the neck radius. These results extend the construction throughout the embedded unduloid family and yield compact equilibria of every sufficiently large mass, with reference neck radii converging to any prescribed interior value as the mass tends to infinity.

papers.title: A compact, interrogable Tree Tensor Network Jet Tagger on Lund declustering trees
papers.summary: Jet taggers built on the Lund declustering tree encode QCD radiation structure in the inputs and process it with graph networks. We ask whether the tree itself can also constrain the computation, and what becomes accessible when it does. For this, we construct a novel quantum-inspired Tree Tensor Network (TTN), where a single tensor core is shared among the internal nodes of the Cambridge/Aachen declustering tree, employing Lund coordinates, and with no particle-identification or detector-level information. The construction is based on a strong prior on the radiation history rather than on the constituents, complementary to compact equivariant taggers. Because the same learned map acts identically at every node, the trained model can be evaluated on truncated trees and its latent space compared across recursions, and used to localise where on the Lund jet plane the Pythia and Herwig jet representations diverge, showing the regions of generator-dependent concentration. The $χ=8$ model has 4014 trainable parameters against approximately 391,000 for LundNet. We evaluate boosted top tagging and quark/gluon discrimination at particle level on Pythia and Herwig samples, in both native (Pythia$\to$Pythia) and transfer (Pythia$\to$Herwig) configurations. Despite differing in capacity by two orders of magnitude, the TTN reaches native performance close to LundNet in quark/gluon discrimination, slightly underperforming in top tagging, with a similar Pythia-to-Herwig transfer behavior in both tasks. Finally, we show the behavior of the network as a function of the bond dimension, and as a function of the perturbative scale.

papers.title: Endpoint Compactness and Finite-Energy Weak Solutions for the 2D Isothermal Compressible Navier-Stokes
papers.summary: We prove global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the 2D isothermal compressible Navier--Stokes equations in bounded $C^2$ domains with no-slip boundary conditions. The initial data are arbitrary in the natural energy class, allowing vacuum and unbounded density. This resolves the isothermal endpoint $γ=1$ of the classical 2D finite-energy renormalized existence theory for power-law pressures. We develop a new endpoint compactness argument based on a truncation-independent integrable bound for centered density oscillations. This argument yields strong $L^1$ compactness of the approximating densities at the natural energy level.

papers.title: Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model-Skill Co-Evolution
papers.summary: Skills, reusable procedural guidance added at inference, can substantially improve LLM downstream performance (Li et al., 2026). Prior work retrieves skills from a bank by semantic relevance, then uses them as inference-time patches or for model distillation. The individual utility of each skill, however, is largely neglected. We first show that, in on-policy distillation where skill-conditioned policies serve as teachers, fewer than 25% of retrieved skills provide useful distillation signals. We then propose SGUID, a method for selecting a compact subset of skills for distillation. SGUID retains a skill only if it consistently yields effective learning signals during training. The selected skills are then distilled to produce a better model. Our results show that not all skills are worth distilling. Across four models from the Olmo and Qwen families, distilling 6 selected skills matches or exceeds full-bank distillation in mean avg@12 on three of the four models, and on all four after a second round that distills 3 newly selected skills, while the full banks are up to 11x larger. Importantly, SGUID supports stable model-skill co-evolution: after a distillation round, a new candidate bank is curated from the updated model's rollouts, and SGUID selects which skills to internalize next. In the second round, this loop selects 3 new skills and improves Qwen3-8B from 64.3% to 66.3%. The selection step is essential for stability: on Qwen3-4B, naively updating the model with unfiltered skills degrades performance, including a 0.3 percentage point drop on HMMT25, whereas SGUID improves HMMT25 by 0.5 points after the first round and 1.1 points after the second. These results identify skill selection as the key mechanism for stable model-skill co-evolution.

papers.title: Compact and Efficient Indexes for Learned Sparse Retrieval
papers.summary: This paper investigates how to substantially reduce the memory footprint of learned sparse retrieval indexes without sacrificing the efficiency of state-of-the-art retrieval data structures. Building on SEISMIC, we revisit both levels of its design: the inverted index used to select candidates and the forward index used to score them. For the inverted index, we replace costly per-block summaries with medoids, namely existing documents elected as block representatives, collapsing the per-block metadata from a sparse vector to a single document identifier. For the forward index, we compress both components and values. We reorder the vocabulary to place co-occurring components closer together and encode the resulting $Δ$-gaps with DOTPACKING8, a SIMD-friendly bit-packing scheme that fuses decompression with dot-product evaluation; values are quantized with compact per-component 4-bit codebooks fitted to each component's distribution. We further introduce JUMPDOT, a blocked dot-product kernel tailored for queries that contain only a few non-zero entries. Our forward-index compression is independent of SEISMIC and can be plugged into any system relying on forward-index-based scoring, as we demonstrate by integrating it into KANNOLO. A comprehensive evaluation on MS MARCO with three state-of-the-art learned sparse encoders shows that our solutions markedly improve the speed-space trade-off of learned sparse retrieval: at equal accuracy, our indexes answer queries up to 5.3x faster than the best competitor while using about 3x less memory, and in the most memory-constrained regime, they remain up to 1.9x faster while using up to 3.9x less memory.

papers.title: MiniWAM: Learning Compact Future Targets for Efficient World-Action Modeling
papers.summary: World modeling has emerged as an effective co-training objective for robot policies, giving rise to World Action Models (WAMs) that jointly predict actions and future states. However, most WAMs predict future states in the native representation space of pretrained visual backbones, resulting in high-dimensional targets with substantial training cost. We introduce MiniWAM, which instead predicts compact future representations learned from privileged current-future transitions. To construct these targets, we propose Predictive Representations via Inverse Spatiotemporal Modeling (PRISM), which combines inverse-dynamics supervision with feature reconstruction to emphasize control-relevant transition information while preserving useful future-state information. With the learned PRISM encoder frozen, MiniWAM is trained to jointly predict the resulting targets and robot actions from current observations. With 65$\times$ fewer native future feature tokens, MiniWAM consistently outperforms native future-feature prediction with both DINOv3 and WAN2.1 VAE features, while achieving up to an 8$\times$ speedup in world-action training. At 0.25B parameters, MiniWAM is already competitive with substantially larger WAMs on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin 2.0 simulation benchmarks. Representation analyses further show that PRISM contributes behavioral structure beyond feature reconstruction alone. These results demonstrate that effective world-action modeling does not require predicting native visual futures, and that compact predictive representations provide a strong and substantially more efficient target for policy learning. The project page is available at: https://j1dan.github.io/MiniWAM.

papers.title: Countable compactness is $A$-invariant
papers.summary: Let $A(X)$ denote the free Abelian topological group over a Tychonoff space $X$. We prove that if $A(X)$ and $A(Y)$ are topologically isomorphic and $X$ is countably compact, then $Y$ is also countably compact. Thus countable compactness is an $A$-invariant and, consequently, an $M$-invariant; this answers Open Problem~7.10.1 of Arhangel'skii and Tkachenko.

papers.title: The size of the poset of compatible locally quasi-convex topologies on locally compact abelian groups
papers.summary: For a Hausdorff locally quasi-convex abelian group $G$, let $\C(G)$ be the poset of all Hausdorff locally quasi-convex group topologies on its underlying group having the same continuous characters as $G$. We prove that, whenever $G$ is non-precompact, $\C(G)$ contains an order-isomorphic copy of $(\Pow(\cont),\subseteq)$, where $\cont=2^{\aleph_0}$. The embedding takes values between the Bohr topology and the original topology. Consequently, every infinite discrete abelian group $D$ satisfies $|\C(D)|=\width\C(D)=2^{2^{|D|}}$. The discrete reduction for locally compact abelian groups then yields exact cardinality and width formulas for all such groups; in particular, both invariants equal $2^{\cont}$ for every non-compact $σ$-compact locally compact abelian group. These results answer Questions 6.1--6.3 and 6.5--6.7, and the locally compact case of Question 6.4, posed by L.~Außenhofer and D.~Dikranjan in \cite{AD20}. The embedding also applies to non-compact complete metrizable locally quasi-convex groups. A non-compact precompact nuclear group with a unique compatible topology shows that non-compactness alone does not suffice in the nuclear setting. Finally, the compatible poset of $\R^{\N}$ is not order-isomorphic to that of any discrete abelian group.

papers.title: Testing Extra-Dimensional Gravitational-Wave Polarizations with Compact-Binary Observations
papers.summary: Extra spatial dimensions arise naturally in theories beyond four-dimensional general relativity (GR), but direct observational evidence remains elusive. Gravitational waves offer a distinctive probe: geometric projection onto the observable three-dimensional spatial subspace can produce apparent tensor, vector, and scalar polarizations. We consider one additional spatial dimension and a two-mode tensor-wave ansatz for which the projected polarization components are fixed linear combinations of the same two underlying GR tensor waveforms. These components enter the measured strain through the standard detector antenna patterns. A frequency-domain Bayesian analysis of five compact-binary events constrains two rotation angles for two noncommuting orderings of rotations that preserve propagation within the observed subspace. Two events are further analyzed for four orderings that allow propagation to tilt into the extra dimension. For GW250114, the maximum GR quantiles among the tested rotation orderings are $Q_{\mathrm{GR}}\simeq0.6\%$ for the two-angle fits and $Q^{\mathrm{marg}}_{\mathrm{GR}}\simeq4.6\%$ for the three-angle fits after marginalizing over the third angle. Across the full event sample, the GR reference point lies inside the estimated 90% highest-posterior-density region in every case.

papers.title: Weighted Gagliardo--Nirenberg Inequalities of Grushin Type: Symmetries, Compactness, and Optimizers
papers.summary: In this paper, we study a family of weighted Gagliardo--Nirenberg interpolation inequalities associated with Grushin--type operators on $\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^m$. Specifically, we examine how to control the weighted norm $\||x|^βu \|_{L^B}$ by balancing fractional derivatives $D_x^s u$ with weighted derivatives $|x|^b D_y^r u$. Using two--parameter scaling, spatial translations, and Littlewood--Paley decompositions, we map out exact parameter conditions and demonstrate that the scaling exponents are both necessary and optimal. For multi-parameter weighted extensions, we leverage Khintchine-type random sums to show why $Q \ge 2$ is strictly required. When $x$ and $y$ are radially symmetric, two key advantages emerge: the allowable parameter range for the weights expands, and compact embeddings of the energy space into $L^p$, $2 < p < B$, are completely restored. We establish this compactness through two complementary tools, geometric covering arguments and a generalized three--norm version of Strauss's lemma, that yields explicit pointwise weighted decay estimates. Finally, in the scale--invariant case $β=0$, a concentration--compactness analysis proves that the inequality's sharp constant is achieved by an optimal function, with minimizing sequences remaining precompact up to the natural three-parameter group of symmetries.

papers.title: Uniform Approximation for Operator Learning on Compact Sets
papers.summary: We study uniform approximation for operator learning on compact subsets of Banach spaces. We bound the recovery dimensions and the number of network parameters in terms of compact-set complexity, the target gauge, and recovery stability. For bounded linear operators with a separable domain, we characterize gauge approximability by coordinate decompositions with a common vanishing gauge and arbitrarily small additive errors. Their partial sums give a fixed family of nonlinear encoder--decoder pairs. We prove that nonlinear recovery with a common vanishing gauge and a rank bound depending only on the model dimension is equivalent to the uniform approximation property (UAP). We also obtain linear recovery estimates with the same rank bound and an operator version for the linear factors of nonlinear targets. For Barron operators taking values in a Banach space $Y$ of type $p\in(1,2]$ and admitting a Bochner-integrable density, sampling gives the rate $N^{-(1-1/p)}$ for the expected $L^p(λ;Y)$ error, where $λ$ is a probability measure on the input compact set. For fixed finite-dimensional factors and a class of Hölder maps, we obtain matching upper and lower parameter bounds at fixed sufficiently large depth. Classical sampling and truncation examples provide explicit recovery maps, and a nonlinear integral operator illustrates the parameter bounds.

papers.title: Compactness and Consistency: A Conjoint Framework for Deep Graph Clustering
papers.summary: Graph clustering is a fundamental task in data analysis, aiming at grouping nodes with similar characteristics in the graph into clusters. This problem has been widely explored using graph neural networks (GNNs) due to their ability to leverage node attributes and graph topology for effective cluster assignments. However, representations learned through GNNs typically struggle to capture global relationships between nodes via local message-passing mechanisms. Moreover, the redundancy and noise inherently present in graph data may easily result in node representations lacking compactness and robustness. To address these issues, we propose a conjoint framework CoCo, which captures compactness and consistency in the learned node representations for deep graph clustering. Technically, our CoCo leverages graph convolutional filters to learn robust node representations from both local and global views, and then encodes them into low-rank compact embeddings, thus effectively removing the redundancy and noise as well as uncovering the intrinsic underlying structure. To further enrich the node semantics, we develop a consistency learning strategy based on compact embeddings to facilitate knowledge transfer from the two perspectives. Our experimental results indicate that our CoCo outperforms state-of-the-art counterparts on various datasets.

papers.title: An optimal pinching theorem on compact minimal submanifolds in the Euclidean spheres via eigenvalues of fundamental matrices II
papers.summary: Let $M^n\subset S^{n+m}$ be a compact minimal submanifold of the unit sphere, and let $λ_1\geq\cdots\geqλ_m\geq0$ be the eigenvalues of its fundamental matrix. We prove that $\sum\limits_{α=1}^{\min\{n,m\}}λ_α+λ_2\leq n$ forces $M$ to be a totally geodesic subsphere, a generalized Clifford torus, or a Veronese manifold. We first show that equality everywhere in the pinching condition forces the second fundamental form to be parallel. Next, by computing the eigenvalues of the fundamental matrices of irreducible symmetric $R$-spaces, we obtain a complete classification of the equality cases among minimal submanifolds with parallel second fundamental form.

papers.title: FastJEV: Understanding Redundancy for Compact JEV Inference
papers.summary: JEV models make multimodal decisions by directly scoring candidates. Although the common context is encoded once, candidate evaluation can still repeat matching token histories, duplicate inference states, and execute the full backbone. In this paper, we study these sources of redundancy and present FastJEV for compact candidate evaluation. We jointly organize history reuse and state storage, since sharing computation requires preserving states for later branches. We first introduce shared context anchoring to reuse recurrent initial states and omit unused final recurrent caches. We extend this reuse through candidate prefix sharing, retaining the intermediate states needed by subsequent branches. To further reduce the depth of these paths, we apply decision guided pruning based on relative score changes measured on a small unlabeled set. Our method retains full context encoding and all candidates without additional training. We evaluate FastJEV across three OmniJev model sizes on five public benchmarks and reconstructed LIBERO-10 offline questions. At the selected pruning budgets, the complete method reduces candidate depth by 43.75% to 45.83%, while retaining 93.66% to 97.52% of the original task scores on average across the six evaluation sets. Through controlled experiments, we show how candidate overlap and branching structure affect the execution cost of history reuse. In our implementation, candidate prefix sharing can reduce repeated computation while increasing latency. These findings motivate designing sharing granularity and execution schedules together for efficient JEV inference.

papers.title: A Counterexample to Two Compactness Conjectures of Brudnyi
papers.summary: We construct a quasi-Banach function lattice $X$ on $\mathbb R$ whose quasi-norm is order continuous and invariant under every translation. Nevertheless, $X$ contains a bounded sequence with common compact support which is equicontinuous in $X$ and has no norm-convergent subsequence. This provides a counterexample to Conjectures 2.5 and 2.11 proposed by Brudnyi in \cite{Brudnyi2015}.

papers.title: Noise-Induced Navigation in Non-convex Domains and Compact Manifolds
papers.summary: In this note, we study the problem of designing a feedback law that globally steers a system to a prescribed target configuration. Even if the system is fully actuated, topological obstructions generally prevent the existence of globally asymptotically stabilizing continuous feedback laws. We revisit this problem in a stochastic setting by allowing noise to enter through the control channels. Using a criterion for asymptotic stability in the large that combines local Lyapunov stability with positive recurrence, we constructively show that one can construct elementary feedback laws that achieve global asymptotic stability in the large, of the target equilibrium point in connected Euclidean domains with obstacles and manifolds without boundary. For Euclidean domains with obstacles, we also show that the method extends naturally to the problem of finding the minimizer of a strongly convex function with non-convex constraints. Numerical experiments illustrate the effectiveness of the approach for Euclidean domains with circular obstacles and the two dimensional sphere. Additionally, we study the role noise strength when there is a non-convex obstacle, in which case the system might show metastability.

papers.title: CORAL-KV: Compact Cross-Layer Prediction and Residual Coding for Autoregressive Video KV Caches
papers.summary: Autoregressive video diffusion models maintain a growing attention key-value (KV) cache, making memory a key bottleneck for long video generation. Recently, clustering-based quantization has emerged as an effective method to compress video KV caches by grouping similar key and value vectors then quantizing residual errors. However, when later frames attend to the compressed history, small reconstruction errors can compound as the video grows. Beyond the within-layer similarity exploited by clustering, we find strong dependencies across cache layers in video models. This motivates Coral-KV - Calibrated Offline, Residual-coded, and Adapted Locally - a KV-cache compression framework that uses cache states in each layer to predict keys and values in subsequent layers, then quantizes the remaining prediction residuals. We construct compact block-diagonal-plus-low-rank (block-DPLR) predictors: block-diagonal components model channel relationships within each attention head, while a global low-rank term models dependencies between heads. Coral-KV exposes a flexible fidelity-memory trade-off: it can reuse its predictors across videos or refit lightweight block-diagonal predictors to the current video for higher fidelity. Across extensive evaluations on both HY-WorldPlay and MAGI-1, our reusable configuration improves PSNR over QVG-4 by 0.32 dB and 4.95 dB, respectively, while using 48% and 37% less cache memory. Against QVG-Pro, our video-adapted configuration improves MAGI-1 PSNR by 3.77 dB while using 33.7% less cache memory. Coral-KV also maintains higher reconstruction fidelity over extended generation and reduces temporal discontinuities while retaining comparable generation latency.

papers.title: Fourier analysis of compact oscillons
papers.summary: We present a new derivation of the exact compact oscillon in the signum-Gordon model using Fourier methods. This approach decomposes the oscillon into an infinite, uniformly convergent series of discrete modes consisting of a fundamental frequency and its odd higher harmonics, in contrast to standard analytic potentials, where the corresponding infinite perturbative series fails to converge. Crucially, our oscillon evades the non-existence theorem for spatially localized, small-amplitude periodic states. We investigate the accuracy of truncating the Fourier series and find that the primary mode alone provides a remarkably accurate approximation of the exact solution, with agreement improving significantly when the first two non-vanishing harmonic modes are included. Furthermore, we generalize this framework to a swaying compact oscillon with a periodically moving boundary. We show that describing such an oscillon requires even-order modes, whose coupling with the odd source terms induces a dynamic modulation that generates the swaying motion, even though the spatial Fourier profiles themselves are time-independent.

papers.title: A weakly modelled view of the joint compact-binary mass plane: population structure and spectral-siren cosmology
papers.summary: We introduce a flexible mixture model for the joint source-frame component-mass distribution of compact binaries, inferred simultaneously with cosmology, together with a framework that identifies structures in the reconstructed density, quantifying their posterior stability, local prominence, and cosmological relevance. Applied to GWTC-5.0, the workflow clarifies several familiar and emergent structures. The $\sim35~M_\odot$ feature is classified as a clear near-equal-mass peak despite an ambiguous interpretation in the primary-mass projection. A weaker unequal-mass concentration near $(21,12)~M_\odot$ is recovered frequently but with lower prominence. A tentative joint transition near $60~M_\odot$ appears at mildly unequal masses, with a more robust manifestation in the primary-mass projection. For cosmology, the two-dimensional mass model constraint on $H_0$ is $33\%$ narrower than a model that flexibly reconstructs only the primary mass, and only $\sim~10\%$ wider than analyses based on strongly parameterized one-dimensional spectral structure. At the feature level, we show that the $\sim10~M_\odot$ and $\sim35~M_\odot$ concentrations depend on $H_0$ mainly through a common scale which captures the entire $\sim~(1+z)$ cosmological rescaling of both masses; the intermediate unequal-mass feature instead retains residual dependence in the orthogonal mass-ratio direction. More generally, we argue that population prominence, formal inclusion in an astrophysical feature catalogue, and cosmological relevance need not coincide. These results suggest that a genuinely two-dimensional view may be required to fully exploit spectral-siren information. Our workflow provides a reproducible way to detect population structure and identify which aspects of its geometry are associated with spectral-siren constraints. The feature finder is directly applicable to other population reconstructions.

papers.title: On Critical Dimensions for Compactness in the Boundary Yamabe Problem, II
papers.summary: We determine the sharp compactness ranges for the scalar-flat and minimal-boundary Yamabe problems on smooth compact manifolds of positive conformal type, excluding the conformal round hemisphere. For zero scalar curvature and positive constant boundary mean curvature, compactness holds through dimension $14$ for general boundary and dimension $21$ for umbilic boundary. For positive scalar curvature and zero boundary mean curvature, the corresponding upper dimensions are $14$ and $20$. Together with the noncompactness examples in Part I, these results identify the transition dimensions in both boundary classes. For positive scalar curvature, we also prove compactness through dimension eight for every fixed real boundary mean curvature, and obtain higher-dimensional ranges when this curvature is near zero or sufficiently large and positive. The proof combines scalar-correction estimates for the full conformal Fermi metric expansion with a geometric formula expressing the logarithmic coefficient of the corrected energy as a negative sum of squares.

papers.title: Compact toric Einstein four-manifolds
papers.summary: This is a continuation of our previous paper on toric gravitational instantons. We develop a systematic theory of compact simply-connected Einstein four-manifolds with toric symmetry. Applications include (1) The construction of simply connected positive Einstein four-manifolds with arbitrarily large $b_2$. Our method is based on local gluing combined with a global virtual counting argument. The key idea involves a particular design of rod structures to enable a gluing construction and restrict possible degenerations. (2) A topological characterization of algebraically special toric Einstein metrics. This uses special curvature identities for $W^+$ in the toric setting. (3) Uniqueness, up to scaling and isometry, on toric four-manifolds admitting algebraically special Einstein metrics. The proofs uses a variational study of the Einstein--Hilbert functional. (4) Diffeomorphism classification of compact toric Einstein four-manifolds in terms of an improved Hitchin-Thorpe inequality $χ\geq3|τ|$. In particular, our construction recovers all the classical toric Einstein metrics, including the Page and Chen--LeBrun--Weber metrics, starting from the round sphere through moduli spaces of conical Einstein metrics.

papers.title: Linear-Time Context Compression with State-Space Encoding
papers.summary: Transformer-based large language models (LLMs) impose substantial computation and memory costs as context sizes increase, motivating methods that compress a context into a shorter representation before inference. Existing soft-prompt compression methods typically use the same Transformer backbone as used in the target model, where producing the compressed representation leads to significant latency overheads. This restricts them to the offline setting where context is compressed once and then reused across many queries. We propose the Boa Compressor, a plug-and-play online context compressor built on a Mamba state-space model (SSM) that encodes arbitrary-length context in a single linear-time pass, producing a representation on which we condition a frozen target LLM. The SSM is trained by distillation, matching the next-token logit distribution from the LLM ingesting the full context (as teacher) to the same LLM ingesting the compressed representation (as the student). At equal compression ratios, Boa matches or surpasses the performance of existing state-of-the-art offline compression baselines, while being an order of magnitude faster than Transformer-based implementations, thereby reducing end-to-end latency rather than adding compression time overhead. We demonstrate that Boa also scales well to longer contexts and to compression ratios as aggressive as 16x. By enabling effective compression that is cheap enough to run on every query at inference time, Boa becomes a practical and general tool for efficient long-context inference.

papers.title: Nullhomotopic equivariant shifts and Borsuk-Ulam-compatible compact abelian groups
papers.summary: We disprove the classical version of the Borsuk-Ulam-flavored conjecture, due to Baum-D{ą}browski-Hajac, that free actions $X\times \mathbb{G}\to X$ on non-empty compact Hausdorff spaces by non-trivial compact groups admit no equivariant maps $X*\mathbb{G}\to X$. Specifically, among non-trivial compact abelian $\mathbb{G}$, the conjecture fails precisely when $\mathbb{G}$ is torsion-free profinite.

papers.title: A faint dust ring beyond the compact disk of Sz 76
papers.summary: We report new ALMA Band 7 high-resolution ($\sim$0.05$^{''}$) continuum and $^{12}\text{CO}\ (J=3\text{--}2)$ observations of the disk around the young low-mass star Sz 76. Visibility-plane modeling reveals a previously undetected, faint outer dust ring centered at $\sim$45 au surrounding the compact central disk. Including this low-surface-brightness feature increases the characteristic dust radius from $R_{\text{dust,68}} \approx 7$ au to $41$ au. Combined with an outer gas extent of $R_{\text{CO,68}} \approx 77$ au, the resulting gas-to-dust size ratio decreases from an extreme value of $\sim$11 to $\sim$2, placing Sz 76 in line with typical protoplanetary disks and contradicting a scenario of unimpeded inward radial drift. These results demonstrate that spatial filtering or limited surface-brightness sensitivity can severely underestimate disk sizes, highlighting the necessity of multi-scale observations to properly identify dust traps and accurately constrain disk evolution.

papers.title: Compactness in Combinatorial Banach Spaces and Beyond
papers.summary: In this paper we are going to discuss compactness in combinatorial Banach spaces. After discussing the definition and structure of these spaces, we proceed to propose compactness criteria for them and for their extensions. Finally, we demonstrate their connection with theory of hypergraphs.

papers.title: The intersection of two real flag manifolds in a complex flag manifold, and the canonical form of a compact symmetric triad
papers.summary: The necessary and sufficient conditions for the intersection of two real flag manifolds in a complex flag manifold to be discrete are stated including a previous known result. The discrete intersection of real flag manifolds is the orbit of a Weyl group, which is an antipodal set of a complex flag manifold. The triple of two real flag manifolds and a complex flag manifold as an ambient space is constructed from a compact symmetric triad. It is shown that the compact symmetric triad can be taken to be canonical.

papers.title: MeshCarve: Artisan Mesh Generation with Flow Matching in Compact Latent Spaces
papers.summary: Prior artisan mesh generation works largely predict face tokens autoregressively, which makes inference slow. Recent methods instead flow match continuous latents built by Variational AutoEncoders (VAEs), but reconstruction quality drops significantly when geometry and topology are jointly encoded, and further when the latent space is compressed. We present MeshCarve, a flow matching method that generates entirely in compact latent spaces, generating vertex positions and edge connections separately and sidestepping the difficulty of a joint compact latent. To shorten the token sequence, we propose a hierarchical sparse transformer backbone, instantiated as VertexVAE and EdgeVAE. Instead of encoding fields over the surface voxels, both VAEs anchor on discrete vertices in their latent spaces, which drastically reduces the token sequence length, and our spatial-aware compression shortens it further without costing reconstruction. VertexVAE directly encodes vertex occupancy. For connectivity, we propose vertex-link encoding, which turns arbitrary connectivity between vertices into fixed-length continuous per-vertex embeddings and recovers complex artistic topology faithfully. MeshCarve combines these VAEs with an anchor generator and flow matches on the shortened token sequences. It shows advantages over state-of-the-art autoregressive and flow matching methods on Objaverse and generalizes to Toys4K. To the best of our knowledge, it is among the first artisan mesh generation methods whose every generative stage runs in a spatially compressed latent, with a token sequence only a fraction of the most compressed previous autoregressive and flow matching works.

papers.title: Regularity and compactness theory of stable free-boundary minimal hypersurfaces
papers.summary: We establish the free-boundary version of Schoen-Simon's regularity and compactness theory for stable minimal hypersurfaces in a complete $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold-with-boundary, following the intrinsic PDE scheme introduced by the first-named author. The key step is to prove sheeting theorems in the two possible scenarios in which local weak flatness can occur near a point on $\partial M$: flatness with respect to $\partial M$, and flatness with respect to a reference hypersurface-with-boundary meeting $\partial M$ orthogonally. We obtain these theorems via $\varepsilon$-regularity results for geometrically adapted tilt functions that quantify flatness while keeping track of the ambient geometry. These tilt functions satisfy nonlinear elliptic PDEs on the hypersurface which are amenable to an intrinsic analysis via De Giorgi iteration, made possible by the weak Caccioppoli-type inequalities obtained from stability. Both results apply to immersed hypersurfaces with a singular set of locally finite $(n-2)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. When specialised to embeddings, they yield compactness and regularity: a sequence of stable free-boundary embedded minimal hypersurfaces with uniformly bounded area and singular sets of locally finite $(n-2)$-measure admits a subsequence converging to a free-boundary minimal hypersurface that is smoothly embedded away from a singular set of Hausdorff dimension at most $n-7$. Convergence is smooth and graphical, possibly with multiplicity, away from this singular set. As an application, we extend to arbitrary dimension the free-boundary Almgren-Pitts existence theory developed by the second-named author with X. Zhou and prove that every compact Riemannian manifold-with-boundary of dimension $n+1$ contains a free-boundary minimal hypersurface smoothly embedded outside a singular set of Hausdorff dimension at most $n-7$.

papers.title: Fixed-point sets of semifree group actions on infinite-dimensional compact convex sets and their manifolds
papers.summary: Let $A$ be the fixed point set of a semifree action of a compact (metric) group $G$ on a Keller space $X$ (an infinite-dimensional compact convex subset of a separable Fr\' echet space). All Keller spaces are homeomorphic and all nontrivial compact Lie groups act on all $X$'s semifreely with unique fixed points (see Section 3). We prove (1) if $A$ is a single point, then it is the fixed point set of a semifree action of $G$ with uniformly small orbits, (2) if $A$ has Property Z (e.g., is of infinite codimension) in $X$, then the action of $G$ may be replaced by one with fixed point set $A$ and uniformly small orbits, and (3) if $A$ is an \ANR, then $G$ acts on $X$ semifreely with fixed point set homeomorphic to any compact (metric) space that is Shape equivalent to $A$. Corollaries are (a) every Cell-like set (i.e., continuum of trivial Shape) embedded in a Keller space $X$ as a Z-set is the fixed point set of semifree actions on $X$ with uniformly small orbits of all nontrivial compact Lie groups (Corollary \ref{CE}) and (b) (a partial converse to a Theorem of P.\ A.\ Smith) if a compact (metric) space $Y$ has the Shape of a compact \ANR, then $Y$ embeds in $X$ as the fixed point set of a homeomorphism of $X$ of period $n$ if it is acyclic in \v Cech homology with $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ coefficients. Finally, we (4) apply recent results of Cappell, Weinberger, and Yan \cite{cwy} to give for a compact manifold $M$ modeled on a Keller space homological and algebraic K-theoretic conditions equivalent to the existence of semifree actions of finite groups $G$ on $M$ with prescribed \ANR\ fixed point sets and (5) generalize (3) to prove that if $A$ is an \ANR\ that is the fixed point set of a semifree action of $G$ on $M$, then every compact (metric) space that is Shape equivalent to $A$ is homeomorphic to the fixed point set of a semifree action of $G$ on $M$.

papers.title: $r$-Process as Production of Lanthanides from Compact Object Mergers
papers.summary: The relative contributions of binary neutron star (BNS) and black hole-neutron star (BH-NS) mergers to the Galactic enrichment from the rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) remain an open question in nuclear astrophysics. In this paper, we present end-to-end numerical simulations of binary population synthesis, nucleosynthesis, and Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) via Compact Object Mergers Population Astrophysics and Statistics (COMPAS), SkyNet network, and a stochastic multi-zone model, respectively.
